About This Job
Working for this large multinational energy business the successful candidate will be responsible for the provision of up to date energy market information to gas and power customers, producing market reports in a timely manner, whilst maintaining an exceptional standard in terms of data accuracy and written commentaries.
The team you would be joining are based on the trading floor itself so you will be operating in a fast paced, high pressure environment therefore excellent communication skills and the ability to perform with 100% accuracy is essential for this role.
Key responsibilities will include:
• The creation and development of a suite of daily and weekly market reports to customers in the European entities:
• Daily reports that display price movements from the previous session and include a commentary discussing market drivers in that session.
• Within Day Updates that show intra-day price movements and a brief market commentary.
• Weekly Reports that provide a week on week comparison of each market and market commentaries explaining the drivers behind the price movements.
• Maintain database of historic prices and supply and demand data, which can be used to produce the above market reports.
• Maintain distribution lists for market reports, ensuring that recipients of reports are legitimate and that new flexible customers receive reports.
• Develop an in depth understanding of European energy markets, with a particular focus on supply and demand fundamentals, as well as drivers from the wider global energy complex.
• The provision of ad-hoc market briefing papers for distribution both internally and externally, in response to major market events and/or changes in the legislative and regulatory environment, in conjunction with the procurement desk.
Ideal qualifications, skill sets and experience:
• Strong academic background with a numerate, technical or energy focused degree.
• Experience in a commercially focus role within a UK gas/power business would be ideal.
• Solid numerical ability and attention to detail/deadlines under pressure.
• Excellent communication skills and telephone manner and confident personality.
• Strong Excel and VBA skill sets.
• Fluency in the German language both verbal and written is essential.
If you have the relevant energy background or career experience skill sets, and would like to know more about the above opportunity, then please apply now.
Due to the amount of applications we receive on a daily basis unfortunately we are only able to respond to the successfully shortlisted candidates. If you have not heard from us within 3-5 days of applying for this position, your application was not successful on this occasion. We may however be able to contact you with a more relevant position at a later date.

Reporting to the Head of Environment & Sustainability, you will define and deliver the environmental strategy for the STEP programme and provide programme-level assurance that environmental and sustainability risks are effectively understood, managed, and controlled throughout the full lifecycle of the power plant.
As a senior leader within UKFE, you will ensure environmental performance is embedded into engineering, construction, operational, and strategic decision-making. You will lead the development of a proportionate, evidence-based Environmental Case and provide leadership across environmental consenting, permitting, regulatory engagement, and sustainability performance.
This is a high-profile position operating in a unique technological environment where regulatory frameworks continue to evolve. Your expertise will help shape how fusion energy is responsibly delivered for future generations.
Key Responsibilities
Environmental Strategy & Programme Leadership
• Define and deliver the environmental strategy across your allocated area of responsibility within the STEP programme.
• Provide senior environmental leadership across engineering, construction, operations, and programme delivery functions.
• Ensure environmental considerations are integrated into programme design, delivery, and operational decision-making.
• Balance innovation with regulatory compliance, environmental stewardship, and societal expectations.
Building Environmental Capability
• Build, lead, and develop a high-performing environmental team capable of supporting a complex, multi-decade programme.
• Provide strategic direction, coaching, and technical oversight to environmental professionals and specialists.
• Promote a culture of environmental excellence, collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement.
• Increase environmental awareness and capability across engineering and delivery teams.
Environmental Case & Design for Environment
• Lead the development and ongoing justification of the programme's Environmental Case.
• Establish frameworks for identifying, assessing, and managing environmental impacts at system and programme level.
• Ensure environmental requirements and Best Available Techniques (BAT) are embedded within engineering and operational decision-making.
• Oversee environmental assessments, modelling, inventories, and supporting evidence required to demonstrate environmental performance.
• Ensure environmental risks are identified, assessed, managed, and visible to support informed decision-making.
Permitting, Consents & Regulatory Strategy
• Define and deliver environmental consenting and permitting strategies.
• Lead all environmental inputs to the Development Consent Order (DCO) process and subsequent permits, licences, consents, notifications, and authorisations.
• Support regulatory engagement activities and act as a senior environmental subject matter expert with regulators, planning authorities, and key stakeholders.
• Ensure all environmental submissions are robust, credible, and capable of withstanding external scrutiny.
• Navigate evolving regulatory frameworks associated with emerging fusion technologies.
• Drive continuous improvement through lessons learned from environmental performance and regulatory engagement.
Leadership & Stakeholder Engagement
• Act as a senior ambassador for environmental and sustainability performance across the organisation.
• Influence programme teams, supply chain partners, contractors, and external stakeholders.
• Represent the organisation confidently with regulators, government bodies, local communities, and industry partners.
• Champion a culture where environmental responsibility and sustainability are recognised as critical to engineering excellence and programme success.
• Foster an inclusive, collaborative, and high-performing team environment.
About You
We're looking for a strategic environmental leader with experience delivering complex, highly regulated infrastructure, energy, nuclear, environmental, or major capital programmes.
Essential Experience
• Significant leadership experience in environmental and sustainability management within a regulated industry.
• Proven track record of developing and delivering environmental strategies for major infrastructure, energy, nuclear, industrial, or engineering programmes.
• Experience leading environmental consenting, permitting, and regulatory engagement activities.
• Strong understanding of environmental impact assessment methodologies, environmental management systems, and environmental risk management.
• Experience integrating environmental requirements within major engineering, construction, or operational projects.
• Demonstrated capability in leading multidisciplinary teams and influencing senior stakeholders.
• Expertise in environmental governance, assurance, and programme-level decision making.
• Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, including engagement with regulators and government bodies.
Desirable Experience
• Experience supporting Development Consent Orders (DCOs) and nationally significant infrastructure projects.
• Knowledge of radiological and non-radiological waste management principles.
• Understanding of Best Available Techniques (BAT) assessments.
• Experience within the nuclear, fusion, energy generation, or similarly regulated sectors.
• Chartered environmental, engineering, sustainability, or related professional status.
What You'll Bring
• Strategic thinking and commercial awareness.
• Outstanding leadership and influencing skills.
• Technical credibility combined with pragmatic decision-making.
• The ability to navigate complexity and ambiguity with confidence.
• A passion for environmental stewardship and sustainable innovation.
• Curiosity, resilience, and a commitment to continuous improvement.
Why Join Us?
This is an opportunity to help create a new energy industry while shaping the environmental standards that will define it.
You will work alongside world-leading scientists, engineers, regulators, and policymakers to ensure fusion energy is developed responsibly and sustainably.
Join us and help deliver clean energy for generations to come.

Qualifications
Essential:
• Degree or equivalent in a relevant subject, environmental engineering or related field.
• Proven extensive experience in the environmental discipline, having worked with large programmes of similar complexity.
• Expert understanding of environmental and sustainability legislation and standards.
• Experience embedding Best Available Techniques (BAT) and Environmental Impact Identification (ENVID) into complex engineering projects.
• A strong understanding of ISO14001 standard &/or other environmental management frameworks including experience in the certification process.
• A strong understanding of project management lifecycle and progressive assurance techniques.
• A confident influencer both verbally and through the production of written report

We’re looking for a Workforce Management Operations Partner Senior Lead to join our Operational team in our London office!
The WFM Operations Partner Senior Lead is accountable for the WFM–Operations partnering model, ensuring Workforce Management disciplines are consistently embedded into operational decision-making across the business.

The WFM Operations Partner Senior Lead is accountable for the people, standards, and decision quality of the WFM Operations Partner function. This includes direct line management of Ops Partner Leads and dotted-line functional leadership over Intraday and Scheduling Specialists.

Act as the direct people manager for WFM Operations Partner Leads, with accountability for:

hiring, onboarding, and role clarity
•
performance management, GrowWise cycles, and calibration

ongoing coaching, feedback, and development.

Set and reinforce clear expectations for:
•
decision quality
•
stakeholder behaviour

adherence to WFM principles and frameworks.

Develop Ops Partner Leads from:
•
metric interpretation

structured decision support

confident, evidence-based challenge of Operations leadership.

Ensure consistent capability, judgement, and behavioural standards across the Ops Partner team through calibration and peer review.

Act as the senior WFM representative to Operations Heads and senior Ops leaders.
•
Own the quality and consistency of workforce decisions taken by Operations.
•
Serve as the final escalation point for workforce-related decisions that materially impact service, cost, or workforce sustainability.

About This Job
Home Care Assistant - Earn from £13.36 p/h in Wolverhampton Wombourne and Kingswinford
Do you want to help people in need and make a difference in their lives? Do you want to work with the elderly, but don't have any experience or qualifications? If so, then becoming a care assistant might be your perfect career.
As someone who cares for others on a daily basis, we know that it can bring huge rewards. And when we say ‘rewarding’, we’re not just talking about pay. As a care assistant, you can make a real difference to the lives of older adults in your local area by giving them the support they need to live independently in their own homes.
Care Assistant Pay & Benefits
•
Flexible Hours Available - 16-20 Hours Per Week
•
Industry-Leading Training
•
Full PPE Protection
•
Care Certification
•
Employee Benefit Scheme
•
Career Development & Progression Opportunities
Becoming a Care Assistant
As one of our care assistants, you’ll be earning minimum £13.36 per hour with industry-leading training and support provided.
You will be required to work alternative weekends and due to the nature of the role, you will need a full UK driving license & access to reliable transportation to visit your clients.
No specific qualifications or background in care is required to become a care assistant. What’s more important is that you have a natural calling to care for people. With this intact, we provide all the training you need o to become one of our exceptional Home Instead CAREGivers.
As well as supporting older adults within their communities, we support employees by providing opportunities such as advanced industry-leading training, employment opportunities & benefits schemes.
This is a fantastic opportunity to join our award-winning, small, family-run, local home care company whose visits always involve a strong element of companionship.
Care Assistant Job Description
This is a totally unique care sector opportunity - We will carefully match you to your own small circle of older adults in your local community and you will support them to live happy, independent lives by providing:
•
Prompting & assisting your clients with their medication
•
Support getting in & out of the shower & getting dressed
•
Help to & from the loo
•
Preparing simple meals and light household duties
•
Companionship, a cup of tea & a natter
•
Shopping tips, social Calls, appointments, clubs hobbies (own car advantageous)
The Benefits of Becoming a Care Assistant
•
Flexible Part-time hours are available between 16-20 hours per week (unfortunately, we cannot offer purely school hours or full-time as each employee only has a small circle of their own regular clients)
•
If you have some availability mornings (ideally starting at 8:00) or tea/evening times (ideally starting at 17:00) & a couple of hours alternate weekends, then this position could fit around your other interests & commitments
•
Excellent training is provided and you’ll meet some like-minded people
•
The biggest benefit of all is making a difference every day and putting a smile on your client’s faces

About This Job
Forget everything you think you know about working in care. We do it differently!
Our hours are flexible and we have no calls under 1 hour. Calls are very often 2/3/4 hours long. You don’t get a schedule that changes every week, you will be allocated clients that match your availability and continue to care for those same clients each week.
We don't just do personal care, we do everything for our clients that you would do for your own loved ones.
Experience is not necessary. We believe in our training not experience. We offer excellent rates of pay and benefits as well as our accredited training developing your talent for caring.
What we can offer you:
• Our calls last a minimum of 1 hour so you can build strong relationships.
• Full training and development.
• No pressure between client visits.
• Excellent pay rates, holiday pay, pension, mileage and employer benefits including Employee Assistance Programme.
What we need from you:
• You must have your own transport available.
• You have availability that covers at least 4 days each week.
• You are willing to help clients with personal care, home help and companionship.
The only skills you need are to be caring and compassionate. So if you are looking for part-time work during daytime, evenings and/or weekends get in touch.

About This Job
QIMA’s rapid growth has added complexity in data, systems, processes, and management structures. Successful integration requires close collaboration between technical, commercial, and core business teams. This role is responsible for driving that collaboration.
The Technical Project Manager, Commercial Integrations is an individual contributor responsible for the end-to-end integration of data, systems, and operational processes from acquired companies into QIMA's core infrastructure. You will own workstreams from initial data discovery and process mapping, through to production-ready pipelines and process handover, coordinating across legal, finance, commercial, and technical stakeholders. This is a mid-level role requiring engineering rigour and commercial fluency in equal measure: genuinely at home with data, and equally able to explain what you are doing and why it matters to people who will never open a database.
Key Responsibilities
Technical Project Management
• Own project plans, timelines, risk registers, and status reporting for all active integration workstreams; escalate blockers and business decisions proactively.
• Maintain integration documentation, decision logs, and handover notes that enable teams to own the output once integration is complete.
Stakeholder Management & Communication
• Coordinate across Legal, IT, Finance, Sales, Marketing, and Revenue Operations to gather requirements, identify dependencies and handoffs, secure milestone sign-off, and manage competing priorities.
• Translate complex data processes into clear, accessible language for non-technical stakeholders at all seniority levels.
M&A Data Integration
• Lead post-acquisition data integration workstreams: discovery, profiling, schema mapping, matching, cleansing, and migration from acquired entities into QIMA systems.
• Define integration plans with clear milestones, dependencies, and acceptance criteria; identify data quality or process issues early and drive well communicated remediations.
• Validate data integrity across source and target systems at each stage; facilitate knowledge-extraction with acquired company experts before systems are decommissioned.
Data Engineering & Automation
• Build or coordinate data pipelines and ETL processes; apply AI and machine learning tooling to accelerate data ingestion, deduplication, and anomaly detection.
• Design automated quality checks that reduce manual validation effort without compromising accuracy.
Master Data Management & Governance
• Apply MDM principles to align acquired data with QIMA master data standards; define ownership, stewardship rules, and lineage documentation for integrated datasets.
• Navigate data protection and privacy requirements throughout integration, ensuring GDPR compliance while preserving data usability for analytics and AI applications.

Qualifications
Required Experience
• 5-7 years in technical project management, including data integration or data engineering, with proven track record delivering complex, multi-stakeholder projects.
• Hands-on experience with schema mapping, data matching and deduplication, ETL design, and data quality validation.
• Working knowledge of SQL; Python or comparable scripting for data processing and automation.
• Understanding of MDM concepts (data domains, golden records, ownership, lineage) and PII regulations (GDPR and equivalent), including the practical balance between compliance and AI usability.
• Experience managing project workstreams across multiple concurrent stakeholder groups spanning commercial and technical functions.
• Exceptional English-language communication skills with proven ability to communicate technical concepts to non-technical audiences in writing and in meetings.
• Bonus: post-merger integration experience, including direct exposure to CRM, marketing automation, or ERP systems in a data integration capacity
• Bonus: project management certification (PMP, Prince2, or Agile/Scrum).
Desired Characteristics
• Clear Communicator: You can make a data mapping discussion accessible to a CFO and credible to a data engineer, and you know which version to use in which room.
• Disciplined with Detail: Integration work lives and dies in the detail. You catch discrepancies before they reach production and document decisions so they are not repeated.
• Technically Grounded, Commercially Aware: You understand data architecture and frame technical work in terms of the outcomes it enables.
• Comfortable with Ambiguity: Acquired data is rarely clean and processes are rarely documented. You impose structure and clarity without being rigid.
• Collaborative by Default: You coordinate large, cross-functional groups without a reporting line through preparation, clarity, and trust.

Additional Information
Does this describe you? Then we want to hear from you as soon as possible! Apply now with your CV in English and we can write the next chapter of the QIMA story together!

About This Job
About the Role
We are looking for a driven Aerodynamics Project Leader to work closely with our Principal Aerodynamicists and take the technical lead of a team of talented engineers. You will own aerodynamic development projects from first concept through to track validation, turning a clear performance objective into a released, manufactured and correlated solution on the car.
This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You will set the direction for your project team, make the calls on where to focus limited CFD and wind tunnel resource, and keep a development programme moving at race-team pace while protecting quality and learning. Just as importantly, you will develop and empower the engineers around you, creating an environment where ideas are challenged openly and the best solution wins.
Working within the constraints of the FIA regulations and the cost cap, you will need to be as smart with your resource as you are with your geometry. Every run, every tunnel hour and every release has to count!
Responsibilities
You will take a project from the first spark of an idea to a part running on the car, turning performance targets into clear objectives and building plans that balance CFD, wind tunnel time, design office capacity and manufacturing lead times against the race calendar. Spotting risks early and dealing with them before they become problems will be second nature.
Day to day, you will:
• Lead concept generation, challenge assumptions about how the car works, and direct CFD exploration with evidence-based decisions on what to pursue and what to park
• Plan and run test sessions in our onsite wind tunnel, analyse results with rigour, and adjust course when the data tells a different story
• Get hands-on in CAD where needed to develop and refine aerodynamic surfaces
• Drive projects through release, working closely with the Design Office, Structures, Composites and Manufacturing teams to protect aerodynamic intent within weight, stiffness, cost and build constraints
• Support the introduction of new parts at the track alongside Vehicle Performance and trackside engineers
Just as importantly, you will bring the project team with you. You will communicate results and theories clearly in a way that encourages challenge, coach and empower less experienced engineers through delegation and honest feedback, and lead post-project reviews so we learn from what worked and what did not. You will also help shape a culture of continuous improvement in our tools, methods and processes.
About You
You are an experienced F1 aerodynamicist who has taken technical projects the whole way from concept to track. You understand the fundamentals well enough to explain the flow physics behind a result, not just the number, and you are comfortable making and defending a decision when the data is incomplete and the clock is ticking.
You will bring:
• Multiple years’ experience in F1 aerodynamic development
• Demonstrable experience leading projects through the full aero development lifecycle, from concept to track
• Familiarity with CFD techniques, including non-standard models
• Experience planning and running wind tunnel programmes, and interpreting CFD, tunnel and track correlation
• A strong working understanding of the ATR and cost cap framework
• Proficiency in CAD for aerodynamic surfaces (preferably NX)
• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with a proven ability to develop less experienced team members

Additional Information

Atlassian Williams F1 Team is an equal opportunity employer that values diversity and inclusion. We are happy to discuss reasonable job adjustments.

About This Job
We're looking for a Staff Researcher to join the Mitigation Platform team in London and help advance Wise’s mission to build an open, fair financial system for everyone, everywhere.
At Wise, our mission is clear: money without borders. We build for people and businesses living global lives, and we are entering an exciting stage of that journey. As Wise scales, the systems we build internally need to scale with us.
The Mitigation Platform team is building the foundational platform that teams across Wise will use to design, launch, and improve mitigation experiences. This role will ensure that platform is grounded in real team needs, adaptable across regions, and capable of enabling faster, more consistent, higher-quality work across Wise.
Your mission:
We're looking for a Staff Researcher to join our Mitigation Platform Squad. You'll help build the foundational platform that teams across Wise use to design, launch, and improve mitigation experiences at scale.
You'll be working with cross-functional partners and dig into the needs and behaviours of internal teams and agents to uncover what's truly common across mitigation workflows, what needs to stay team-specific, and where platform-level solutions can create the most leverage.
For this role in particular, the emphasis will be on shaping broader platform questions: how teams should escalate cases across departments, how much flexibility the platform should offer, what a strong default handling experience looks like, how AI and LLM-powered solutions should fit into agent workflows, and where Wise can cut duplicated effort across teams.
This is a Staff-level role for someone who thrives in ambiguity and sets research direction rather than waits for it — you'll define the questions worth answering in a vast problem space, choose the right methods to answer them, and translate what you learn about complex operational systems into product strategy the platform team can act on. You'll connect fragmented knowledge across teams into a coherent picture no single team can see, and use it to influence decisions well beyond your immediate squad.
You'll also join a thriving community of 20+ researchers in London. While embedded in teams and squads across the company, they come together regularly to learn from and support one another.
As a Staff Researcher, you'll contribute by:
•
Setting priorities and research direction - proactively prioritise your work, understanding how the work connects to squad and business goals.
•
Demonstrating strong craft and capabilities - lead by example when it comes to complex evaluative and generative research, and raise the bar for quality and rigour when non-researchers on your squad take it on themselves.
•
Articulating now, next, and future - balance the long-term platform vision with what the team needs to learn next quarter, formulating and adapting research plans as the space takes shape.
•
Driving impact through your work - leverage your research insights to actively shape what our product looks like today and where it should be headed in the future.
•
Influencing senior leaders - skilfully negotiate with teams, squads and senior leaders across the organisation to drive user-centred decision making.
•
Leading with guts - set ambitious goals and hold yourself to them, while championing quality, our users, and a human-centered approach to product development
•
Bringing judgment to AI - leverage AI to accelerate research delivery where it genuinely helps, and bring that same judgment to the product itself: shaping how AI and LLM-powered workflows should serve agents
A bit about you…
Research excellence:
•
Strong judgment and systems thinking: matching research approach to the level of ambiguity, from greenfield generative exploration to focused evaluative studies, and seeing patterns across teams that others miss.
•
Skilled at building decision confidence through well-designed studies and clear evidence, delivered in bite-sized insights teams can act on immediately.
•
Proven track record of scaling research influence across teams and senior stakeholders.
•
Experienced with mixed-method research, and thoughtful about where AI tools accelerate the work.
•
Top-notch storytelling: you’re able to connect complex operational work to real customer impact.
•
You work with urgency by pushing projects forward and quality up, rather than perfecting reports
Strategic impact:
•
Able to articulate research strategy, define what success looks like, and positively influence squad and team focus.
•
Comfortable establishing and tracking metrics that show whether the platform (and the research behind it) is actually working.
•
Deep understanding of how research ladders up to team, squad, and business goals, with a track record of proactively spotting opportunities rather than waiting to be asked.
•
Skilled at influencing outcomes among senior stakeholders with strong opinions, negotiating well while keeping relationships positive.
•
A track record of mentoring non-researchers to run quality research, and raising the quality bar as they do.
As a heads up, this role probably isn't for you if:
•
Your experience is primarily market research and/or academia
•
You don't have demonstrable experience leading UX research within the tech/product industry
•
You haven't mentored or coached others in research before
•
You prefer working at arm's length — this role is embedded in a squad's day-to-day, not consulting from the sidelines
•
You're not comfortable navigating ambiguity across multiple product areas in a fast-paced environment

Additional Information
For everyone, everywhere. We're people building money without borders  — without judgement or prejudice, too. We believe teams are strongest when they are diverse, equitable and inclusive.
We're proud to have a truly international team, and we celebrate our differences.
Inclusive teams help us live our values and make sure every Wiser feels respected, empowered to contribute towards our mission and able to progress in their careers.
If you want to find out more about what it's like to work at Wise visit Wise.Jobs.
Keep up to date with life at Wise by following us on LinkedIn and Instagram.

• Act as a trusted advisor to senior executives on strategic technology decisions and business‑architecture alignment.

About This Job
Talan is recruiting for an IT Application Support Analyst to join the London-based CIT Business Support Team dedicated to the Commodities-Indexed Transactions Group (CIT).
This is on-site 5 days a week.
CIT provides liquidity and market-making services across commodity markets to a large and diversified base of clients worldwide. Products include Base and Precious Metals, Oil, European and North American Power and Natural Gas, Coal, Emissions and Agricultural Commodities.
The CIT Business Support Team is one of two CIT IT sub-teams; the other team is the CIT Core Development Team.  Both teams work on the trading floor in close partnership with CIT.  The primary responsibility of the Business Support Team is to provide front-to-back production support for the CIT platform.
Key Responsibilities
As a member of the team, support the global commodities in house platform, critical for front-to-back functionality including pricing, risk management, market data sharing, p&l reporting, settlements, physical scheduling, trade confirmations and regulatory reporting.
Key daily tasks include:
•
Proactively monitoring the system
•
Configuring the system
•
Analysing and resolving production support technical and functional issues
•
Fielding questions from all  CIT personnel including traders, marketers, risk managers, and middle office and keeping them informed of system issues and changes affecting them
•
Logging incidents
•
Advising the core development team of necessary bug fixes and enhancements
•
Participating in the first-line support rota, which includes an early shift for resolving overnight batch issues and an on-call system for overnight and weekend support.  The rota allows those not engaging in first-line support to focus on more in-depth analysis.
•
Release management

This role requires strong problem-solving and communication skills.  The analyst will engage directly with many different teams within the bank including trading, sales, middle office, back office, confirmations, market risk and accounting.  Therefore, the ability to pick up diverse product and process knowledge will be critical.
Functional skills

Front to back process.
•
Knowledge on commodities/PNL/Pricing is a plus.
Technical skills
•
Intermediate level relational database and SQL skills are required.
•
Python or other programming skills
•
Infrastructure - Windows infrastructure / servers - essential

Good knowledge of script languages (Powershell …) and Windows environment.

Maintain a comprehensive framework for challenging and tracking remediation plans for control gaps and/or elevated residual risks identified during assessments

Partner with the Analytics team to enhance data reporting, dashboards, and quality.

Design and drive adoption of metrics and indicators for quarterly reporting.

Prepare high-quality materials, dashboards, and trend analysis for senior management and risk committees.

Significant experience leading Financial Crime risk assessments in a complex financial institution, including multi-entity or multi-region scope.

Demonstrated ownership of risk assessment methodology design, including scoring models, materiality, and control effectiveness integration.

Proven ability to effectively communicate with Product, Analytics, and 2LOD Compliance and Risk teams.

Strong capacity to prioritize tasks, maintain a problem-solving mindset, and take ownership to drive and deliver projects from inception to completion with high attention to detail

About This Job
Turner & Townsend is a global professional services company with over 10,000 people in 50 countries. Collaborating with our clients across real estate, infrastructure and natural resources sectors, we specialise in major programmes, programme management, cost and commercial management, net zero and digital solutions.
We are passionate about making the difference, transforming performance for a green, inclusive and productive world.
As well as helping organisations deliver and integrate new assets as quickly and efficiently as possible, we help set the asset strategies that support their corporate objectives. We also work with our clients to create safe and comfortable environments which are inexpensive to maintain, sustainable and practical to conduct business from.
OUR CORE VALUES
• We love a challenge
• We are stronger together
• We bring out the best in everyone
To support and progress our values, we:
• Developed a market leading suite of bespoke digital tools to deliver our market leading cost management services: The Hive
• Are a champion of a diverse workforce and culture
• Offer role development and advancement opportunities
• Set out our NewLeaf strategy, commitment to social value and environmental issues
• Provide opportunities for professional development (working with industry leading professionals, RICS Chartership development support, NEC accreditation)
• Offer a level of independence with multidisciplinary collaboration and support where needed
We want our people to succeed both in work and life. To support this we promote a healthy, productive and flexible working environment that respects work-life balance. We believe that everyone should pursue their passions and provide a real opportunity for this; whether you join one of our sports teams, social networks or bring a new interest to your colleagues.
MAIN PURPOSE OF ROLE
• To perform the role of the Commission Manager, taking responsibility for end-to-end service delivery
• To ensure that client objectives are met through the delivery of an effective cost management service
SCOPE
Cost Managers handle commissions of varying sizes, depending upon the complexity of the project. Typically, projects fall within the £5m to £10m range. Our markets include Healthcare, Education, HT&M, Retail Banking and beyond.
KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES
Commission Management, to include:
• Assisting on feasibility studies and writing procurement reports
• Estimating and cost planning to include producing and presenting the final cost plan, utilising the relevant cost management tools and services utilising The Hive
• Tendering and procuring, including managing the pre-qualification stage, producing the tender list, producing the preliminaries, tender analysis, producing the tender report and compiling the contractual documents, utilising the relevant cost management tools and services; The Hive; eTender Platform
• Conducting the role of contract administrator, including dealing effectively with post contract cost variances and the change control processes, where applicable referring major changes to line manager
• Taking personal responsibility for making cost checks and carrying out valuations on larger projects and in all cases ensuring that timely and accurate cost checking and valuation takes place
• Producing monthly post contract cost reports via our Cost Control App and presenting them to the client
• Inputting into value engineering
• Negotiating and agreeing final accounts
• Interfacing with the client, Project Manager, and other consultants, at all project stages
• Work collaboratively with Turner and Townsend’s project management team during project delivery
• Where appropriate, leading a cost management team, ensuring that they deliver on all of the above accountabilities
• Utilising our full suite of bespoke digital cost management tools and services; The Hive: Benchmarking App, CostX, Market Rates App, eTender Platform, and Cost Control App
• Implementing our Embodied Carbon Calculator, a bespoke carbon accounting tool, to produce carbon footprint reports
• Supporting the execution of our NewLeaf strategy
• Management of internal fees, internal job costing and resourcing requirements
Marketing and business development, to include:
• Identifying opportunities to develop new business with existing clients and reporting such opportunities to the appropriate line manager and by making effective use of the marketing database
• Developing and maintaining a professional network of peers and potential clients
• Assisting in the production of bid documentation
• Identifying ways in which cost management procedures, templates and products can be improved and referring ideas to the appropriate line manager
• Being involved in extracurricular activities including external groups, attending networking and CPD events
Internal management accountabilities, to include:
• Knowledge management – Ensuring that key information and learning generated from each commission is input into the Turner & Townsend internal database
• Process improvement – Identifying ways in which internal systems and processes can be improved and referring ideas to the appropriate line manager
• Assist in the support, development, and mentorship of junior staff members
REPORTING
Depending upon context, a Cost Manager is likely to report to a Senior Cost Manager, or Associate Director.
KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS
A Cost Manager will in part be assessed by the extent to which:
• Commissions are managed to the right quality standards and are completed efficiently and on time
• Service delivery on commissions is in line with the conditions of appointment
• Good relationships are developed with clients and members of the cross-functional team
• They work as an effective member of the cost management team, including where appropriate, taking effective responsibility for Assistant Cost Managers
• Opportunities are identified to develop new business with existing clients
• Margin levels are kept track of on all commissions
• Key information and data is effectively cascaded and appropriately retained

Qualifications
We would expect candidates to demonstrate the following:
• Ability to work with autonomy
• A self-motivated individual who is able to take initiative and deliver to tight deadlines
• Working towards or recently achieved Chartered Status
• Have a confident and professional manner
• Highly organised and ability to prioritise own workload
• Ability to collaborate and build relationships across the business
• Ability to work well under pressure
TURNER & TOWNSEND:
We actively encourage applications from all sectors of the community.
SOX control responsibilities may be part of this role, which are to be adhered to where applicable.
Experience and Skills
• A proven track record of delivering high quality cost management / quantity surveying services across the full project lifecycle
• Ideally professionally qualified (RICS or similar)
• Degree or HNC l

About This Job
As a Security Architect, you'll partner with government, financial services, and private sector clients to design security solutions that address their most complex digital risks. You'll translate threat landscapes, compliance obligations, and business constraints into practical security architectures, working across the full engagement lifecycle, from threat modelling, security options analysis, through to facilitating design sessions with delivery teams and presenting recommendations to architecture review boards and senior stakeholders.
Whether that's defining a zero-trust approach for a government department, designing security controls for a bank's cloud migration, or guiding development teams through secure-by-design decisions, you'll bring both depth and pragmatism. Your background in cloud security, application security, and public sector compliance means clients can trust your advice on what works in enterprise environments.
You'll join our central architecture practice alongside experienced Technology Principals and Solution Architects. Security in delivery teams is often under-served; your role is to change that, not through gates and sign-offs, but by embedding security thinking early and keeping it there. That includes guiding and upskilling delivery teams on secure-by-design practices, helping engineers and product managers build security literacy without slowing down delivery.

Qualifications
Essential Requirements
You'll have designed and validated security architectures for enterprise-scale programmes, across cloud platforms, application security, identity and access management, and system integration. You can point to successful outcomes and take clear ownership of the security design decisions that got there.
Cloud and application security; experience securing workloads on AWS and/or Azure, including network segmentation, IAM, encryption, secrets management, and security monitoring. You understand AppSec practices including secure SDLC, SAST/DAST tooling, API security, and container security in agile delivery contexts.
Experience directly working with clients and senior stakeholders to assess risk, facilitate threat modelling, and build consensus around security approaches. You communicate clearly with both technical teams and non-technical leadership.
Highly Desirable
GOV.UK and public sector compliance: experience working within GOV.UK digital standards, GDS service assessments, NCSC guidance, and UK government security classifications (Official, Secret). Familiarity with DSP Toolkit or equivalent assurance frameworks.
Financial services security: experience designing controls for regulated financial environments, including FCA/PRA expectations, PCI-DSS, and secure integration patterns for core banking or payment systems.
Security frameworks and standards: working knowledge of NIST CSF, ISO 27001, CIS Controls, or SABSA. Holds or is working towards CISSP, CISM, CCSP, or equivalent.
GenAI security: experience assessing and mitigating risks in AI/ML solution architectures, including data exposure, prompt injection, model supply chain, and output integrity.

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/ifs1/7440001426.description_excerpt:
About This Job
You'll be designing for people whose work actually matters: maintenance engineers, field service technicians, operations planners working in environments where the software either helps or gets in the way. The stakes are real and the problems are hard, which is exactly what makes this role interesting.
At IFS, product design means owning the full problem, not just the screens. You'll work in a cross-functional squad alongside engineers and product managers, with the scope and support to do the work properly. From problem framing through to something shipped and measured.
But the deeper question is harder than that. The industries IFS serves (field service, asset management, manufacturing, supply chain) are changing faster than the software that runs them. By 2030, we're not confident the interface paradigms we rely on today will still be the right ones. AI, ambient computing, voice, autonomous systems: any of these could fundamentally change how an operations planner or a field engineer interacts with software, or whether they interact with it at all.
That's not a problem we've solved. It's the problem you'd be working on.
What you'll do
Product Design
•
Own design for defined feature areas end-to-end — from problem framing through to production-ready Figma files, with a clear rationale for every decision
•
Work in a cross-functional squad with engineers and PMs, making real decisions rather than executing on someone else's brief
•
Present design thinking to stakeholders with confidence — handling pushback with evidence, not just conviction
Discovery & Research
•
Plan and run user interviews, JTBD analysis, and journey mapping independently — turning findings into clear design direction, not just a readout
•
Track quantitative signals alongside qualitative insight, and use both to drive iteration
AI & Emerging Technology
•
Design AI-driven features with a clear understanding of where AI helps and where it introduces risk — prompts, fallbacks, and human-in-the-loop moments included
•
Bring a genuine perspective on how the interfaces we're building today might become obsolete — and what should replace them
Design Systems & Quality
•
Contribute to the IFS design system by proposing reusable components and patterns rather than designing one-offs
•
Apply WCAG 2.1+ accessibility standards from the start, and design for edge cases, error states, and real-world data — not just the happy path
You'll know it's working when your work ships, holds up in the field, and raises the bar for the next thing. Concretely: task success rates improve, UX-related support tickets drop, and the squad reaches for your work as a reference rather than a starting point.

Qualifications
You may be a good fit if you:
•
You have at least eight years of end-to-end product design experience — from discovery through to shipped product — and you can point to work that reflects real ownership, not just execution
•
You're comfortable running your own research: planning the study, conducting interviews, synthesising findings, and turning them into a clear design direction
•
You know how to work in a cross-functional squad — making real decisions alongside engineers and PMs, not waiting to be handed a brief
•
You know Figma well and have the visual craft to back your thinking up
•
You treat accessibility as a design constraint from the start, not a checklist at the end
•
You've thought seriously about what AI means for the interfaces you build — not just as a feature to add, but as something that changes the fundamental design problem
•
You measure your work — task success rates, support ticket volume, adoption — and use those signals to drive the next iteration
Strong candidates may also have:
•
Experience shipping AI-driven features — prompts, fallbacks, human-in-the-loop moments — not just awareness of the concepts
•
Familiarity with design tokens, contribution models, and what it means to design for a system rather than a screen
•
Some exposure to quantitative signals: task success rates, funnel data, or A/B results — and a habit of using them

Additional Information
We embrace flexibility and hybrid work opportunities to support diverse needs and lifestyles, while also valuing inclusive workplace experiences. By fostering a sense of community, we drive innovation, strengthen connections, and nurture belonging. Our commitment ensures you can work in a way that suits you best, while also engaging with colleagues to share ideas and build meaningful relationships.

A bit about us
Big ambitions. Personal investment. That’s Beyond the Ordinary.
Ready to start your career, learn by doing and see where your ambitions could take you? Welcome to the Audit School Leaver Apprenticeship at BDO.
The programme starts on Monday, 20th September 2027, for an organisation-wide induction (you need to be able to attend). For Edinburgh and Glasgow roles you will start on the 30th August 2027.
We’re the only UK mid-market organisation with more than £1bn in turnover and 8,000 people. Audit at BDO gives you the chance to get involved and build experience from day one. Our Audit teams work across specialist areas including Pension Audit, Public Sector, Not-for-Profit, Financial Services and Technology Risk Assurance, giving you the chance to learn how different organisations work from the inside out.
You’ll be trusted to contribute early, but you won’t be expected to know everything straight away. You’ll learn alongside experienced colleagues, build your confidence through practical experience and have people around you to answer questions and help you develop.
It’s a place to turn big ambitions into a career, with people personally invested in your growth from the start.
And a bit about Audit
Over four years, you’ll gain hands-on experience while working towards your ACA, CFAB or ICAS/Robert Gordan University qualification. You’ll learn through challenging Audit work, build relationships with clients and develop technical, personal and commercial skills as your experience grows.
Starting your career straight from school is a big step, so support is part of the experience too. You’ll join a trainee community, work towards your qualifications alongside your peers and learn from colleagues at different levels across the organisation.
Our early careers people talk about being trusted with client work earlier than they expected, while having supportive teams around them and feeling comfortable asking questions as they learn.
You’ll build your career foundations by doing the work, with the coaching and support to help your confidence grow. When you complete the programme, there’s a permanent role waiting for you.
As for you
You’re curious, resilient and ready to learn. You enjoy solving problems, thinking things through and getting involved.
You don’t need to arrive with all the answers. Bring your ambition and willingness to learn, and we’ll give you opportunities to build your experience, confidence and skills from there.
Join us in one of the following locations - Birmingham, Bristol, Cambridge, Edinburgh, Gatwick, Glasgow, Guildford, Ipswich, Leeds, Liverpool, London, Manchester, Nottingham, Reading and Southampton.
One thing to note: you’ll need to live within a commutable distance of the office you apply to. Relocation support is not provided, so please consider this carefully before applying. Time together in person matters – whether that’s in the office or with clients. It gives you more opportunities to learn from your team, build relationships and get the most from working together.
Is it for you? To apply, you’ll need:
• Three A-levels (or equivalent) at A*-C (excluding General Studies and Extended Projects), or four Scottish Highers OR Advanced Highers at grade A-B (or equivalent, for example, BTEC Extended Diploma). Please note: we do not use UCAS points. You’ll be asked to provide evidence if you’re successful in securing an offer
• GCSEs at grade 4 and above in Maths and English, or Scottish National 5 grade A-C. You’ll also need to provide evidence if successful
• Commitment to balance study and professional work
• The right to work in the UK (we are unable to provide visa sponsorship for these roles as they do not meet the current minimum salary requirements for sponsorship set by the Home Office. Applications from candidates who have their own legal right to work within the UK must cover the duration of their 4-year training contract and employment)
• For the roles based in Edinburgh or Glasgow you will need to be residing in Scotland
How the interview process will go
We want you to know what to expect, so here’s the typical process:
• Online application form.
• Online assessments.
• Video interview.
• Virtual assessment centre.
• Final interview in person.
We’ll keep you updated at each stage and share resources to help you prepare. And just so you know: we don’t use AI in any part of our candidate screening process. Every application is reviewed by a real person.
What you get in return
Our benefits are designed to support your life in and outside of work, with options including additional leave, gym membership and employee discounts, alongside pension, health and wellbeing support and a range of protection benefits.
Salary
£26,615 - £28,275 dependable on location.
Closing date for applications is Sunday 15th November 2026.
Before you go
Starting your career is a big step. At BDO, you’ll get the chance to learn by doing, work with clients and build strong foundations for where you want to go next.
You’ll bring the big ambitions. You’ll have people around you investing in your learning, confidence and development from the start.
Big ambitions. Personal investment.
That’s Beyond the Ordinary.
Apply now.

Job Title
Delivery Lead
Job Description
So, who are we?
IG Group is a FTSE 100 fintech operating across five continents, serving over 1.4m customers and handling billions of dollars in transactions – built on scale, trust, and proof. We didn't pivot to innovation; it's how we've always operated. What that means for the people who work here is real: genuinely complex problems to solve, the technology and resources to tackle them properly, and the kind of scope that's rare in established businesses.
The bar is high – bring a curious and forward-thinking mindset and we'll give you the platform to define what comes next.
Join us at IG – the future gets built here.
Your Team:
This role sits within the new Product Operations team, reporting into the Product Operations Lead, and is deployed onto specific high-priority initiatives as and when they arise, working alongside the Product Managers and Engineering Leads of every squad involved. You'll also work closely with the Product Governance Specialist and Product Partnership Manager where an initiative touches governance approval or third-party contracts, and you'll feed initiative-level status into the Product Operations Lead's wider portfolio reporting and forums such as the Product Development Monthly.
Your role in the Team’s Success:
This is a role for someone who thrives on the big, complex, cross-cutting initiatives that don't fit neatly inside a single squad or even a single domain - platform migrations, new product line launches, multi-quarter strategic programmes that touch several product areas at once. As Delivery Lead you will own the end-to-end delivery of these initiatives, orchestrating multiple Product Managers, Engineering Leads, and squads toward a single outcome. This is a role within a product-led organisation where we need people who are focused on outcomes, not just governance and milestones.
What you’ll do:
Cross-squad and cross-domain orchestration
• Own the end-to-end delivery plan for major initiatives that span multiple squads and/or multiple product domains, sequencing work across teams that don't normally plan together.  Support teams to carve deliverables/plans into manageable slices, making sure value can be found in each slice.
• Identify and actively manage dependencies between squads and domains - the handoffs, shared components, and sequencing constraints that a single squad's Product Manager can't see or resolve alone.
• Bring together the right Product Managers, Engineering Leads, and other stakeholders at the right moments, without taking over their squads' day-to-day delivery.  Help to foster a psychologically safe working environment where people can raise problems, solve issues and find solutions.
Programme-level risk and issue management
• Maintain a single, honest view of risk, issues, and critical-path dependencies across the whole initiative, escalating early and clearly to the Product Operations Lead and senior stakeholders.
• Resolve conflicts where squads have competing priorities or constrained shared resources, making trade-offs visible rather than letting them cause silent slippage.
• Own contingency and mitigation planning for the risks that could derail a multi-team initiative — not just track them on a log.
Stakeholder alignment and communication
• Act as the single point of accountability for "how is this initiative actually going" — able to give senior stakeholders, up to and including the Product Development Monthly forum, a clear and credible answer at any point.
• Keep Product Managers, Engineering Leads, and other functions (Compliance, Legal, Data) aligned to a shared plan and timeline, even when their day-to-day priorities pull in different directions.
• Translate initiative complexity into simple, decision-ready updates for senior leadership.
Technical and delivery credibility
• Bring a high level of technical fluency to understand system dependencies, integration points, and engineering trade-offs across multiple domains.
• Apply sound programme and project management discipline (planning, milestone tracking, RAID management) appropriate to initiatives that are often unprecedented and don't fit a standard template.
Contribution to Product Operations
• Feed lessons learned and delivery best practice back into the Product Operations Lead, helping the wider team get better at running complex, cross-cutting initiatives.
• Support the Product Operations Lead with ad hoc portfolio-level analysis or reporting when capacity allows between initiatives.
What You'll Need:
• Significant experience as a Programme Manager, Senior Delivery Manager, or Technical Project Manager, with a track record of delivering initiatives that span multiple teams or workstreams.
• Demonstrable experience managing complex cross-team dependencies and driving them to resolution, not just tracking them.
• Strong stakeholder management skills, including the credibility and gravitas to align Product Managers and Engineering Leads who don't report into you.
• Enough technical understanding to engage credibly with engineering leaders on architecture, sequencing, and trade-offs across multiple systems or domains.
• Excellent communication skills — able to distil a genuinely complex, multi-team initiative into a clear, honest update for senior leadership.
• Comfortable with ambiguity — these initiatives often don't have a standard playbook, and you'll need to build the plan as much as follow one.
• Open to ambiguity - people need a plan, but they we expect you to be dynamic and adaptable when circumstances inevitably change.
Desirable
• Experience in a regulated financial services or fintech environment.
• Direct experience delivering platform migrations, re-platforming, or major organisational/domain restructuring initiatives.
• Programme or project management qualifications (e.g. MSP, PMP, Prince2) — useful context, though real-world judgement on ambiguous, high-stakes initiatives matters more.
• Deep experience of agile ways of working, to work effectively with Product Managers and Engineering Leads running their own ceremonies and backlogs.
The Perks
It really is more than a job. We think like a start-up, but we deliver like a FTSE 100 — so the bar is high, and we won't pretend otherwise. We work hybrid, which means three days in the office. We’ll recognise your talent and make sure that you can still have a life – at work, and outside of it. Networks, committees, awards, sports and social clubs, mentorships, volunteering opportunities, extra time off… the list goes on.
• Competitive salary
• Flexible Benefits Package on top of your salary (12%)
• Private medical cover for you and your family
• Life insurance
• Contribution to gym memberships
• 25 Days holiday, with 1 additional day off to celebrate your Birthday & 2 additional days off a year for voluntary work (28 in total)
• The option to buy or sell holiday days
• A comprehensive global and local onboarding process

HSEQ Management:
• Promote a strong safety culture across vessels with emphasis on “Zero Harm” and proactive risk management.
• Ensure effective implementation of HSEQ policies, procedures, and initiatives.
• Monitor safety performance, KPIs, and trends; initiate improvement actions where required.
• Lead incident investigations, including root cause analysis and Corrective and Preventive actions.
• Ensure timely reporting and proper classification of incidents .
Audits, Inspections & Compliance:
• Prepare vessels for internal and external audits.
• Participate in audits and inspections; ensure closure of findings within agreed timelines.
• Maintain oversight of vessel certification and statutory compliance.
Marine Operations:
• Monitor and support day-to-day marine operations of assigned LNG vessels.
• Ensure compliance with company SMS, international regulations, and industry best practices.
• Review passage plans, cargo operations, and critical operations as required.
• Provide guidance on navigation, cargo handling, mooring, and emergency preparedness.
Training & Crew Support:
• Provide guidance and mentoring to Masters and Senior officers.
• Support crew competence development, including familiarization and drills.
• Review crew matrix and support compliance with terminal and charterer requirements.
Documentation & Continuous Improvement:
• Review and update company procedures based on operational feedback.
• Ensure effective use of digital tools (e.g.,  Mariapps, ERBs).
• Drive continuous improvement initiatives across fleet operations and HSEQ  performance.
Emergency Response:
• Act as part of the Emergency Response Team (ERT) as required.
• Provide support during incidents and emergencies.
Qualifications
Education & Certifications:
• Certificate of Competency (CoC) – Deck (STCW II/2 – Master Mariner ).
• Relevant training in LNG or Tanker operations
• ISM/ISO Lead Auditor certification will be an advantage.
Experience:
• Candidates must have demonstratble experience in a comparable HSEQ role, with responsibility for HSE management systems, regulatory compliance, risk management and continuous improvement initiatives
• Sailing experience as Chief Officer on tanker vessels (Oil or Gas) is essential, candidates with Masters sailing experience will be prefered.
Skills & Competencies:
• Strong knowledge of Tanker (Gas ,Oil or Chemical )  operations, marine regulations, and industry standards.
• Strong knowledge of HSEQ systems, incident investigation, and risk management.
• Experience with audits and inspections (SIRE, PSC, Flag, TMSA).
• Excellent leadership and interpersonal skills with ability to collaborate with global teams and influence shipboard teams.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities.
• Effective communication skills (written and verbal).
• High level of professionalism, integrity, and commitment to safety.
• Proficiency in digital systems and reporting tools.
Work Conditions:

Position Summary:
The Logistics Coordinator is responsible for coordinating customer shipments and preparing the required import & export documentation, ensuring accuracy, timely processing and compliance with relevant import/export requirements and internal procedures.
The role involves close coordination with customers, freight forwarders and customs brokers, as weel as supporting compliance and audit activities through accurate documentation and effective operational controls.
Main duties and responsibilities:
Shipment Coordination
• Arrange and coordinate import and export shipments on behalf of customers.
• Liaise with freight forwarders to arrange the dispatch of goods and provide the required shipping documentation.
• Consolidate customer orders where appropriate to support efficient combined shipping.
• Coordinate with relevant parties to ensure shipments are processed effectively and required documentation is available.
Import & Export Documentation
• Prepare, review and issue relevant import and export documentation, including: Commercial Invoices; Packing Lists; Export Declarations; Certificates of Origin; Air Waybills; Bills of Lading

Audit Support & Internal Controls
• Support internal and external audits relating to import/export activities.
• Verify the accuracy and completeness of relevant shipping and customs documentation as part of audit and compliance activities.
• Support the review of documentation against applicable regulatory and customs requirements.
• Follow established internal control procedures relating to import and export activities.

Education Level: Associates Degree in Relevant Discipline - Desirable
Professional Certification: Not required
Technical Skills: Data analysis and Microsoft (Excel) skills a must.
Experiences:
Previous hands-on experience in import/export procedures
Strong knowledge of Letters of Credit, inspection certificates, Certificates of Origin, and export licenses
Experience working with an ERP system (preferably Oracle)
Proven experience handling customs compliance and regulatory documentation
Other Requirements:
• Customer focused
• Highly organized and strong attention to detail
• Effective prioritisation
• Clear and professional communication
• Ability to coordinate effectively with internal and external stakeholders
• Ability to work effectively in a busy operational environment

Locations: Hybrid working with one of the following locations as primary: Derby, Warrington or Manchester
Our Mission
Our mission is to deliver clean, affordable energy for all. Our Small Modular Reactor (SMR) provides a British solution to a global energy challenge. We are in pole position to become a world leader in SMRs and the UK's premier green export technology.
The Team
The Reactor Island Layout and Installations team is responsible for developing the integrated layouts, modules and installation strategies that sit at the heart of the Rolls-Royce SMR design. Working across a wide range of engineering disciplines, the team combines systems thinking, modularisation and advanced engineering practices to create a plant that is safe, buildable, operable and licensable, whilst supporting our ambitious deployment targets.
The Opportunity
In this context, we are looking for a Senior Layout Engineer - Containment Block to support our Containment Block Layout Manager. Working within the Reactor Island Installations and Assemblies team, you will be responsible for leading the development of an identified layout scope within the Containment Block, covering Mechanical, Electrical and Plumbing (MEP) modules and installation assemblies. This is a critical role that will influence how the plant is designed, manufactured, installed, commissioned and operated throughout its lifecycle.
We'll need you to:
• Leading the development of Containment Block layouts, installation assemblies and modularisation solutions, ensuring designs meet safety, performance, operability and maintainability requirements.
• Coordinating multidisciplinary engineering activities across Systems, Components, Mechanical Handling, Civil, Structural, Architecture, Human Factors, Operations and Supply Chain teams to deliver integrated engineering solutions.

• Developing manufacturing, installation, commissioning and maintenance strategies that support the Rolls-Royce SMR modular build philosophy and overall delivery model.
• Maintaining ownership of technical risks, assumptions, actions and lessons learned, ensuring issues are escalated, managed and resolved effectively.
• Supporting engineering governance and gated design reviews, presenting design solutions and technical recommendations to senior stakeholders and technical authorities.
• Working collaboratively with licensing, safety case and regulatory teams to support the UK Generic Design Assessment (GDA) process and ensure design substantiation requirements are met.
• Producing, reviewing and approving high-quality technical documentation, including engineering reports, design substantiation documents, interface documents and regulatory submissions.
• Supporting continuous improvement initiatives across layout, installation and modularisation activities, incorporating lessons learned and industry best practice into future designs.
• Acting as a visible technical leader within the programme, building strong working relationships across engineering disciplines while promoting collaboration, innovation and delivery excellence.

What We're Looking For
• A degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related engineering discipline, together with Chartered Engineer status or a clear pathway towards professional registration.
• We'll ask about your experience developing complex layout and installation solutions, managing multidisciplinary interfaces and delivering engineering programmes from concept through detailed design.
• Strong understanding of systems engineering principles, including requirements management, engineering governance, technical risk management and design review processes.
• Proven experience coordinating stakeholders and technical specialists across multiple engineering disciplines to achieve successful programme outcomes.
• Experience producing and reviewing technical documentation, engineering reports and design substantiation packages within a regulated environment.
Ideally, you'll also have experience in:
• Layout and routing of mechanical systems, including piping systems, cable management systems and ventilation/HVAC systems within complex industrial facilities.
• Nuclear Fuel Route design, Reactor Island integration, Mechanical Handling systems or other highly integrated nuclear plant systems.
• Supporting Generic Design Assessment (GDA), nuclear licensing activities or equivalent regulatory approval processes.
• Optimising layouts for constructability, operability, maintainability, inspection, commissioning and through-life operation.
• Modular construction methodologies, installation sequencing, offsite manufacture and modern methods of construction.
• Applying engineering judgement to resolve complex technical challenges involving safety, quality, cost and programme considerations.
Location
We offer hybrid and flexible working but will expect regular attendance at one of our offices in Derby, Manchester or Warrington, together with occasional travel to support programme activities, stakeholder engagement and design reviews.

Job title and apprenticeship level
Level 3 Engineering Technician Apprenticeship (Level 3 – Advanced). Opportunities are available across the following specialisms:
• Mechanical Maintenance
• Electrical Maintenance
• Control & Instrumentation Maintenance
• Precision Machining
• Mechatronic Maintenance
About AWE
We’re a team of remarkable people, united by one extraordinary mission: keeping the UK safe and secure. The UK’s independent nuclear deterrent has existed for 75 years to deter the most extreme threats to our national security and way of life, helping to guarantee our safety, and that of our NATO allies.
Our work is critical. We’re delivering Astraea, the next warhead for the UK’s nuclear deterrent and pushing the boundaries of nuclear science and technology. But that’s just part of the story.
We support the UK government in a range of vital areas – from counterterrorism to global nuclear test monitoring to building a world-class community of experts in nuclear science. This is work that protects lives and strengthens national security.
At AWE, you’ll find more than just a job. You’ll find purpose, growth, and a community like no other. Whether you're just starting out or looking to take your career to the next level, this is your chance to learn from the best, develop your skills, and be part of something truly unique.
Be extraordinary at AWE.
About the apprenticeship
Engineering-related disciplines are at the heart of AWE, helping us maintain and develop the facilities, equipment and systems that support our mission to keep the nation safe and secure.
As a Level 3 Engineering Apprentice, you’ll apply through a single Engineering Apprenticeship route. During the selection process, we’ll take time to understand your interests, strengths and aspirations to help identify the engineering pathway that best suits you and aligns with business needs.
Throughout the selection process, you’ll have the opportunity to learn more about our different engineering specialisms, meet members of the teams and ask questions about the pathways available. This will help us work together to determine the area that offers the best fit for your skills, potential and future development.
From the start of your apprenticeship, you will be aligned to your specific engineering pathway, giving you the opportunity to develop practical skills, technical knowledge and industry experience within your specialist area. Through a combination of hands-on training and college study, you’ll build the foundations needed for a successful career.
This apprenticeship may involve travel to off-site training locations. Transport or expenses will be provided where applicable, and applicants should be willing to travel if required.
Following your initial training period, you will complete placements relevant to your pathway, working alongside experienced engineers and technical specialists. You will apply your learning in a real working environment, further develop your technical skills and gain valuable experience supporting live engineering activities at AWE.
Engineering pathways covered by this apprenticeship
The pathway you follow will shape the type of engineering work you learn and the skills you develop. You do not need to know everything about each area before you apply — the selection process will help you learn more about the options and identify where your interests, strengths and potential may fit best.
Mechanical Maintenance
You’ll work hands-on with machinery and mechanical equipment, helping to find and fix faults, replace parts, and keep facilities and equipment running safely and reliably.
Electrical Maintenance
You’ll work with electrical equipment, wiring and systems, helping to install, test, maintain and repair the technology that powers our facilities and equipment.
Control & Instrumentation (C&I) Maintenance
You’ll work with the sensors, instruments and control systems that help monitor and control temperature, pressure, flow and system performance, making sure equipment works as it should.
Precision Machining
You’ll use specialist machines, drawings and measuring tools to make accurate components to the right shape, size and finish, developing precision, attention to detail and practical manufacturing skills.
Mechatronic Maintenance
You’ll work with mechanical, electrical and automated systems, helping to maintain advanced equipment and understand how different engineering areas work together.
Opportunities when you complete your apprenticeship
Following successful completion of your apprenticeship, and subject to business need and your career aspirations, you’ll move into a role within the business, aligned to the pathway you have trained in.
Whatever pathway you follow, you’ll become part of a skilled community, supporting some of the UK’s most unique facilities, equipment, processes and technologies, while continuing to develop your career at AWE.
About you
• A willingness to learn and develop in a hands-on environment throughout your apprenticeship and career
• An interest in practical engineering, technology or finding out how things work
• Good communication skills
• Excellent team working skills
• Awareness of health and safety
• The ability to follow instructions
• A logical and structured approach to problem solving
• A real passion and motivation for this type of work
This role may appeal to you if you enjoy
• Understanding how things work
• Solving practical problems
• Being hands-on and learning by doing
• Working with tools, equipment or technology
• Mathematics, science, engineering or design and technology subjects
• Checking details carefully and making sure work meets a required standard
• Working as part of a team to achieve a shared goal
• Exploring different engineering areas and seeing where your skills and interests could lead.
Entry Requirements
• 5 GCSEs at grade 4/C or above including Maths and English
• Due to the security requirements associated with this apprenticeship, applicants must be British Nationals and be aged 18 or over by 31 August 2027.
If you currently hold a Level 3 Diploma in Engineering or similar, you should consider applying for a degree level apprenticeship.
The benefits
• Starting salary of £16,750, increasing to £24,500 in Year 2, with further annual salary increases throughout your apprenticeship, subject to satisfactory performance and achievement of apprenticeship milestones.
• Market leading contributory pension scheme
• Generous paid holiday entitlement of 270 hours per year, inclusive of Bank Holidays, plus every other Friday off as part of AWE’s flexible working pattern.
• Access to employee discounts portal, with everyday savings on retail, hospitality and leisure
• Employee Assistance Support Programme and Occupational Health…
