Job Description:
The Account Executive is a high-impact, quota-carrying role responsible for generating new business within assigned territories. AEs will spearhead the entire sales cycle — from outbound prospecting and qualification, to conducting discovery, tailoring solution demos, shaping proposals, and managing multi-stakeholder enterprise evaluations. This role will cover UK, Ireland, France, Belgium, Netherlands, Luxembourg, Spain, Portugal, and Italy.
This is a strategic consultative sales role that requires strong business acumen, exceptional communication skills, and the ability to engage retail and supply-chain leaders at every level. AEs work cross-functionally with Product, Marketing, Partnerships, Customer Experience, and Professional Services to deliver value-driven outcomes.
The ideal candidate has experience selling enterprise SaaS solutions to complex organizations, thrives in a fast-moving environment, and is passionate about helping customers improve inventory accuracy, operational efficiency, and loss prevention effectiveness.
Role Responsibilities:
NEW BUSINESS GENERATION – 35%
• Meet or exceed quarterly and annual revenue targets.
• Identify and qualify new business opportunities through outbound prospecting, inbound follow-up, industry events, and partner engagement.
• Build and maintain a strong pipeline of enterprise and mid-market retailers, distributors, and integrators.
• Strategic territory planning to maximize coverage and accelerate deal flow.
CONSULTATIVE SALES & DISCOVERY – 25%
• Conduct deep discovery to understand customer pain points, operational workflows, and desired business outcomes.
• Translate customer challenges into clear, prescriptive value propositions.
• Navigate complex buying committees including operations, IT, supply chain, loss prevention, and executive stakeholders.
• Tailor ClarityRFID solutions to each customer’s unique environment.
SOLUTION PRESENTATION & PROPOSAL MANAGEMENT – 20%
• Deliver compelling product demos and presentations that communicate ClarityRFID’s value and differentiation.
• Collaborate with Product, Professional Services, and Partnerships teams to craft technically accurate, scalable proposals.
• Lead commercial negotiations including pricing, terms, and contract structure.
• Guide customers through POCs, pilots, ROI modeling, and solution validation.
CROSS-FUNCTIONAL COLLABORATION – 10%
• Work closely with Marketing and Demand Generation on targeted campaigns and regional initiatives.
• Collaborate with Global Partnerships Manager on hardware/SI partner opportunities and joint GTM efforts.
• Align with Customer Experience and Professional Services on customer needs, expectations, and successful handoff post-sale.
• Provide actionable feedback to Product Management on feature requests and market trends.
REPORTING, FORECASTING & PIPELINE MANAGEMENT – 10%
• Maintain accurate CRM data including pipeline hygiene, forecasting, and activity tracking.
• Provide visibility into deal strategy, next steps, risks, and timeline.
• Support weekly, monthly, and quarterly sales reporting and planning.
REPORTING STRUCTURE
Reports to: CEO
Direct Reports: 0
EXPERIENCE & EDUCATION
• Bachelor’s degree in Business, Marketing, Technology, or equivalent experience.
• 3–7 years of experience as an Account Executive or Sales Executive in SaaS or enterprise technology.
• Experience selling into retail, supply chain, logistics, or IoT/RFID ecosystems is highly preferred.
• Demonstrated success closing complex, multi-stakeholder, multi-location deals.
• Proven track record of consistent quota achievement.
Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities
• Strong consultative selling skills with the ability to map solutions to business outcomes.
• Excellent communication and presentation skills, comfortable speaking with C-level executives.
• Ability to navigate long sales cycles and complex buying processes.
• Highly organized, self-motivated, and capable of managing multiple deals simultaneously.
• Strong collaboration skills across Product, Engineering, Partnerships, and Customer Success.
• Understanding of SaaS metrics (CAC, ARR, expansion) and pipeline discipline.
• Comfortable working independently in a global, remote-first environment.

Regular

This is an Audit position ideal for someone with 1-2.5 years of Audit experience in the Financial and / or Operational Audit area.
Job Description
Responsibilities:
Participate as active members of the engagement team throughout each phase (i.e., planning, execution, and reporting). With our standard engagement cadence, the individual in this role will gain broad exposure to our businesses and processes. Work collaboratively and independently to conduct audits across operational, financial, regulatory, and/or technology areas across the Company. Works with moderate guidance in own area of knowledge.
Core Abilities:
What You Deliver
•
Executes aspects of the standard internal audit process, which includes the three phases of planning, execution and reporting out to business management.
•
Performs thorough inquiry and data analysis to understand business operations and assist in developing project scope.
•
Contributes to overall planning efforts for engagement timeline and approach.
•
Examines records, documents, methods, policies, costs, and other factors to determine if functional areas are conducting operations in accordance with established policies/procedures, best practices, United States Generally Accepted Accounting Principles, and governmental and legal requirements.
•
Applies appropriate audit procedures to the areas reviewed to ensure that controls are tested and all significant risks are addressed.
•
Prepares clear and well-organized audit work papers documenting root-cause, work performed, investigation summaries, and recommendations.
•
Formulates appropriate conclusions and clearly documents findings based on testing results. Combines knowledge of Company operations with testing results to determine control effectiveness.
•
Identifies audit findings and considers corrective actions.
•
Identifies opportunities for improvement to audit methodology, tools, and training.
•
Supports department objectives and performs other duties and responsibilities, as assigned.
•
Consistent exercise of independent judgment and discretion in matters of significance.
•
Other duties and responsibilities as assigned.
How You Deliver
•
Conducts audit activities with both internal and external customers in mind when identifying control issues.
•
Stays current on relevant business risks (e.g., current events, audit trends, cyber security, etc.).
•
Utilizes creative thinking, individual initiative, and flexibility in prioritizing and completing tasks.
•
Demonstrates the ability to work in a complex, dynamic, diverse, and fast-paced environment.
•
Demonstrates ownership for assigned activities and is accountable for completing activities and/or requesting assistance as needed.
•
Acts in accordance with stated internal audit and company policies and practices, and maintains the highest degree of integrity in all activities and interactions.
•
Displays regular, consistent, and punctual attendance. Able to work nights and weekends, variable schedule(s), as necessary.
How You Partner
•
Exhibits strong interpersonal skills including written and verbal communications, and an ability to collaborate with others.
•
Shows respect to other team members and clients in all interactions.
•
Demonstrates a willingness to assist other team members in areas outside of direct assignments, when necessary.
•
Collaborates in a virtual environment to complete projects with team members in various locations. However, the employee must be available for extended hours, as needed, and be willing to travel with little notice on occasion.
How You Develop
•
Exhibits a commitment to continuously self-improve by working with leadership to leverage strengths and focus on areas of development.
•
Gains knowledge of basic data analytics and cyber security concepts.
Educational, Experience, and Skill Requirements:
•
Bachelor’s Degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Business, and/or related Business field(s) of study
•
CIA, CPA/Chartered Accountant, or CISA certification is a plus.
•
2 years of experience, internal and/or external audit experience is preferred.
•
Knowledge of Cable, Media, or Telecom industry experience is a plus.
•
Experience working with data analytics, cyber controls, and/or robotic process automation (RPA) tools is a plus.
•
Out-of-town travel approximately up to 20%.

Let’s go on an adventure together!
Hey there, we’re G Adventures. We’re one of the world’s leading small group travel companies, and we’ve always believed that travel isn’t just about where you go — it’s about how it changes you.
For the last 35 years, we’ve set out to do things differently. No cookie-cutter tours. No giant buses or cruise ships. And not to mention, as few selfie sticks as possible. Quarry Operative - Class 2 HGV Role
Furzebrook, Dorest

The Role
We are seeking a reliable and safety-conscious Class 2 HGV Driver to join our team based at Furzebrook.
In this role, you will be responsible for operating a Class 2 LGV rigid tipper vehicle, transporting quarry materials safely and efficiently between the production face, processing plant, storage facilities, and customer delivery locations. The majority of your work will involve moving material from the quarry to designated tipping bays for processing, with occasional deliveries to dockside and storage facilities at Poole Quay to support shipping operations.
What You'll Be Doing
• Safety First: Carry out all duties with health and safety as the highest priority, ensuring compliance with company policies, site rules, and safe systems of work at all times.
• Operate a Class 2 LGV rigid tipper vehicle from the Furzebrook operating centre, transporting materials safely and efficiently between the quarry, processing plant, designated storage areas, and customer delivery locations.
• Conduct comprehensive pre-use vehicle inspections at the start of every shift, identifying and reporting any defects immediately and taking appropriate action to ensure the vehicle remains safe and roadworthy.
• Transport pit grades from the quarry to the processing site, tipping material into designated bays for processing. When required, transport material directly from the quarry to dockside facilities or covered storage at Poole Quay to support shipping operations.
• Ensure full compliance with all Road Transport Regulations, including Drivers' Hours, Working Time Directive requirements, and Tachograph regulations, maintaining minimal infringements.
• Download and submit Digital Tachograph Driver Card data on a weekly basis in line with company requirements.
• Attend and maintain Driver CPC training, ensuring the required 35 hours of periodic training is completed within each five-year cycle and keeping all qualifications up to date.
• Maintain the vehicle to a high standard by regularly cleaning external areas, the tipper body, and removing any retained material where necessary.
• Keep the vehicle cab clean, tidy, and presentable at all times.
• Take responsibility for ensuring the vehicle is in a fit, safe, and roadworthy condition before and during operation.
• Adhere to all company procedures, site rules, speed limits, and prevailing road or site conditions, operating the vehicle in a safe and professional manner.
• Report any changes to driving licence status, endorsements, or other relevant driving-related information promptly.
• Accurately complete all required documentation, vehicle records, and compliance paperwork as required.
• Represent the company professionally when interacting with customers, site personnel, contractors, and members of the public.

• Valid Class 2 HGV (Category C) Driving Licence.
• Valid Driver CPC Qualification Card.
• GCSEs (or equivalent) in English and Math.
Essential Skills & Experience
• Minimum of 1 year experience driving HGV Class 2 vehicles.
• Strong understanding of Drivers' Hours Regulations, Tachographs, and the Working Time Directive.
• Commitment to maintaining high standards of health and safety.
• Good communication skills and the ability to work independently.
Desirable Experience

• Experience working within a quarrying, aggregates, mining, or construction environment.

Registered Veterinary Nurse
Salary: Circa £30,000 DOE
Location: City Vets, Heavitree, Exeter
Job Type: Permanent
Looking for more than “just nursing”?
If you’re an RVN looking for a role where you can develop your clinical skills, gain excellent exposure to a busy main centre and become part of a highly supportive nursing team, this could be the opportunity you’ve been looking for.
At City Vets, our nursing team is at the heart of what we do. We are a progressive, ambitious team who give our nurses the opportunity to take on responsibility, develop their interests and get involved in a much broader range of clinical work than traditional nursing duties.
Our main centre in Heavitree is an RCVS-accredited practice, supported by three nearby branch practices in Alphington, St Thomas and Whipton. Across the group, you’ll have exposure to a large and varied caseload, modern equipment and a team of experienced colleagues who genuinely want to help you progress.
Why City Vets is different for nurses
This is a role where you’ll get excellent exposure to a busy, varied clinical environment.
You’ll work alongside a supportive team of 12 vets, 9 RVNs and dedicated support staff, with experienced lead nurses available to guide and mentor you. For a newly qualified RVN, or someone looking to develop their skills within a busy main centre, this provides the perfect balance of support and opportunity.
Our nurses are trusted to do far more than traditional day-to-day nursing duties. You’ll have opportunities to develop your skills in:
• Stage 1 dental procedures
• Nurse-led outpatient CT
• Advanced imaging and patient preparation
• Anaesthesia and inpatient care
• Dental imaging and procedures
• Nurse-led consultations
• Minor procedures, including lump removals
• Supporting complex and interesting cases
• Exotic patient care
We also have dedicated dentistry expertise within the practice, alongside CT, ultrasound, digital radiography, endoscopy and dental imaging. Our separate wards for dogs, cats and exotics mean you’ll gain exposure to a broad range of patients and clinical presentations.
Interested in exotics? Even better.
If you have an interest in exotic nursing, there is plenty here to get excited about.
We see a varied exotic caseload and have nurses with experience and further qualifications in exotics. You’ll have the opportunity to build your knowledge and confidence with exotic patients while working alongside colleagues who are happy to share their experience.
Our practices are also proud to hold Cat Friendly Clinic accreditation through the ISFM, while St Thomas holds Silver Rabbit Friendly accreditation through the RWAF and Heavitree is a Gold Standard RWAF practice.
A team that wants you to progress
We believe that being supported doesn’t mean being held back.
Our nursing team is structured to give you access to experienced lead nurses and Clinical Nursing Managers, with clear opportunities to develop your skills and progress internally. If there’s an area of nursing you’re passionate about, we want to help you explore it.
Whether your interests lie in dentistry, imaging, anaesthesia, exotics, inpatient care or consultations, we’ll support you to develop your career in the direction that suits you.
We already have multiple nursing certificate holders across exotics, anaesthesia, imaging and dentistry, and we actively support our team with further qualifications and CPD. We offer extensive internal and funded external CPD because we believe investing in our nurses ultimately means better care for our patients.
Great facilities. Great caseload. Even better support.
Our Heavitree main centre is extremely well equipped, with:
• CT scanner
• Ultrasound
• Digital radiography
• Endoscopy
• Dental imaging
• Separate wards for dogs, cats and exotics
• Dedicated dentistry facilities
We also benefit from certificate holders across the wider veterinary team, visiting specialists in cardiology, ophthalmology and physiotherapy, regular CPD events and dedicated input from Cave Veterinary Specialists. We work closely with local referral hospitals, giving our team excellent clinical support when cases require it.
Your wellbeing matters too
We want you to build a rewarding career without sacrificing your life outside work.
Our out-of-hours service is outsourced, helping to protect work-life balance, while inpatient care remains in-house during our normal working arrangements. Weekend duties are shared fairly across the veterinary team.
And then there’s Exeter itself  with the coast, estuary, moors and countryside on your doorstep, alongside a vibrant food scene and excellent transport links to London and beyond.
What we’re looking for
We’re looking for an RVN who is:
• Motivated and keen to develop clinically
• Passionate about delivering excellent patient care
• Confident or keen to develop as a consulting nurse
• Interested in learning from a varied and interesting caseload
• A strong team player who enjoys working collaboratively
• Committed to providing an excellent client experience
• Interested in developing additional clinical skills
• Interested in exotics advantageous, but not essential
Whether you’re newly qualified and looking for the right environment to build your confidence, or an experienced RVN looking for greater responsibility and progression, we’d love to hear from you.
What we offer
• Circa £30,000 salary, depending on experience
• 5 weeks’ holiday plus bank holidays and birthday leave
• Relocation support
• RCVS and VDS fees paid
• Employer contribution pension scheme
• Generous staff discount scheme
• Life assurance
• E-car salary sacrifice scheme
• Enhanced equal family leave
• Extensive internal and funded external CPD
• Genuine opportunities for clinical development and progression
Ready to take your nursing career further?
If you’re looking for a role where your skills will be valued, your development will be supported and you’ll have the opportunity to do more, City Vets could be the right fit for you.
Come and join a nursing team where nurses really are our superpower.

The Role
We are looking for a Data Engineer who will be a key member of the Service Delivery team, responsible for designing, building, and maintaining scalable data pipelines and data products that support analytics and operational decision-making across the organisation.
This role is critical in ensuring data is reliable, accessible, and aligned to business needs, working across a variety of data sources and platforms to deliver high-quality, production-ready solutions.
The successful candidate will have strong technical expertise combined with excellent communication and problem-solving skills. They must be comfortable working across teams, translating requirements into robust technical solutions, and managing data pipelines end-to-end.
Pragmatic, data-driven, detail-oriented, and self-motivated are essential traits for success in this role, along with a mindset focused on scalability, reliability, and continuous improvement.
What You’ll Do
- Design, build, and operate end‑to‑end ETL/ELT pipelines across ingestion, transformation, and serving layers.
- Architect scalable, reusable data pipelines and frameworks that balance performance, cost, and reliability.
- Implement incremental loads, schema evolution, and data contracts to ensure stable, production‑grade pipelines.
- Monitor and maintain pipelines, including logging, validation, alerting, and incident response.
- Collaborate closely with BI, analysts, and architects to ensure datasets meet business requirements, SLAs, and reporting needs.
- Lead complex incident investigations and root‑cause analysis, driving remediation and prevention.
- Review and improve code, pipelines, and models to ensure quality, maintainability, and reuse.
- Translate requirements into technical designs with clear constraints, SLAs, and acceptance criteria.
- Mentor junior engineers and contribute to standards, patterns, and best practices across the team.
What You’ll Bring
- Strong ownership mindset: ability to move from task execution > pipeline ownership > system design accountability.
- Ability to balance scale, latency, cost, and governance when making design decisions.
- Solid communication skills to:
- Explain technical trade‑offs clearly to technical and non‑technical stakeholders
- Provide proactive updates on risks, changes, and dependencies
- Align teams across engineering, BI, and business domains
- Structured and proactive working style:
- Deliver maintainable solutions with strong documentation and observability
- Identify issues early and escalate appropriately
- Drive continuous improvement in reliability and engineering practices
- Strong problem-solving capability:
- Diagnose complex failures and data issues systematically
- Build reusable patterns to reduce duplication and operational load
- Mentoring mindset:
- Guide junior engineers
- Improve team quality through reviews, standards, and shared practices
Technical Skills
- Data Modelling: Designs analytical data models for multiple consumers, understands schemas, keys, and data grain, and balances normalisation versus performance using established and reusable modelling patterns.
- Data Governance: Embeds governance into pipeline and data model design, including lineage, traceability, ownership, and data quality rules, while ensuring alignment with data classification and compliance requirements.
- ETL / Data Engineering: Designs, builds, and operates end-to-end ETL/ELT pipelines, including incremental processing, idempotent patterns, and schema evolution, with a focus on scalability and reliability.
- Development (SQL / Python): Writes clean, optimised SQL and scalable Python code, applying modular design, logging, testing, and code review practices, while considering performance and scalability trade-offs.
- Data Products / BI Integration: Designs and delivers datasets and data products with clearly defined SLAs, ensuring compatibility with BI tools and alignment with reporting and analytics requirements.
- Data Quality & Testing: Implements automated validation, schema checks, and monitoring, and leads investigations into data quality issues to identify root causes and prevent recurrence.
- Architecture & Scalability: Makes informed design decisions across batch vs streaming and ETL vs ELT approaches, building reusable, scalable components that improve platform efficiency and reliability.
- Security & Governance: Applies security-by-design principles, including access controls, data masking, and compliance enforcement, and supports audits through strong traceability and documentation.

We’re here to lead the modal shift, helping businesses transition from road to rail with confidence, clarity, and measurable impact.

SEGA is one of the leading interactive entertainment companies in the world, with our European HQ based in West London and development studios spanning the UK and Bulgaria. Known for quality and creativity above all else, our studios include Sports Interactive, Two Point Studios, Hardlight and Creative Assembly.
At the heart of SEGA is our publishing team based in London, where we help the studios bring their creative vision to life. Here we have a hardworking bunch of people spanning Tech, Sales, Marketing, Finance, QA and more.
Together, we drive the continued success and evolution of our Western business through living our company values of being product focused, embracing true partnerships and always having fun so that we can strive to come together as One SEGA.

Location: SEGA Europe, Chiswick Business Park, London
Role Summary
As a Localisation QA Language Specialist, you will play a key role in maintaining the linguistic quality and accuracy of SEGA titles, ensuring localisation meets the company’s standards and player expectations. Working in close collaboration with LQA Project Managers and the wider Localisation team, you will provide language expertise across
both in-game code and localised assets, supporting activities such as build sign-off, translation quality assessment, defect quality review. Through close engagement with internal teams and external vendors, the role contributes directly to localisation quality, process consistency, and successful game releases.
Key Responsibilities
•
Provide confidence in the localisation process by delivering translation reviews prior to game implementation and on the code during testing processes.
•
Ensure consistency of the testing process across all vendors by providing regular feedback to LQA PMs. Provide IP support to the vendors as required.
•
Review the code (across all projects) to ensure readiness for testing before it is delivered to the vendor.
•
Review defects and edits from vendors for format, grammar and naming conventions. Identify quality concerns and feedback to LQA PM to resolve concerns promptly.
•
Regularly test play the build with “confidence” checks across all products. Ensuring product quality and delivery progression are maintained.
•
Regularly review terminology within the build to reduce risk of quality issues identified too late in the process.
•
Liaise with the SEGA Territories to create and maintain Localisation CQA Checklists, to be provided to external vendors and complete them internally to mitigate the risk of must-fix issues in the submission code.
•
Formally sign-off the code before submission or release by performing confidence cycles and ensuring that the build meets all the submission and release criteria.
•
Support the business and the Studios with actor selection (casting feedback), review of the samples prior to implementation.
•
Support with urgent translation requests / compliance high risk translation that require immediate implementation (without the need to outsource).
•
Create and maintain language specific documentation for Development and wider business reference, including game glossaries and any related assets.
•
Provide marketing assets review and editing as required.
•
Provide any language related support for the contracted language to the wider business, including AI Prompt support, AI translation quality evaluations and feedback on tool development.
•
Support with vendor selection feedback (for both translation and LQA).
•
Game testing as and when required by the project / business, for instance executing test cases and supporting on GaaS testing according to volume.
Knowledge, Skills and Experience
•
Excellent linguistic knowledge and deep understanding of your contracted language.
•
Understanding of the linguistic trends and consumer expectations of the target market, able to deliver precise, relevant and resonant language for that territory and IP.
•
Knowledge of SEGA IP.
•
Understanding of first party naming conventions.
•
Proficient working knowledge of the software tools in use at SEGA (test case management, text editing tools and general office software).
•
Working knowledge of CAT tools (e.g. MemoQ) and familiarity with AI-driven Localisation and LQA solutions.
•
Clear, concise and professional communicator, both in English and your contracted language.
•
Flexible and adaptable to different LQA tasks and projects.
•
Passion and enthusiasm for the role and the company, capable of motivating and inspiring others.
WORKING THE SEGA WAY
We believe that making the best games relies on having the best people, so we make sure that we look after ours…
•
For our gaming buffs, you can get involved in our lunchtime get gaming sessions in our games lounge and Club SEGA, regular gaming tournaments and free SEGA games on Steam.
•
If you're more of a foodie, you can take advantage of fresh fruit and cereal every single day.
•
Fitness fanatics will love our discounted gym membership, ride to work scheme, workout area and bootcamps in the business park. You can find your zen with weekly yoga classes as well as in-house massage therapy.

We offer competitive salaries and a fantastic bonus scheme so that you can stay motivated and focused on making SEGA the best it can be.
•
We hold regular lunch & learn sessions, company updates at incredible venues in Central London and Christmas parties that you’ll want to brag to your mates about! What’s not to love?

We pride ourselves on having flexible working hours to ensure that you have a life outside of the office.

We want people of all backgrounds to see themselves represented and included in our work, so we actively seek to diversify our team and bring more voices to the table. All applicants are welcome!

Planning, specifying, and implementing manufacturing facilities and processes for motor control unit and harness assembly and testing

Leading equipment specification, procurement, and commissioning activities, including Factory and Site Acceptance Testing (FAT/SAT)

Attending Design Reviews and providing insights into manufacturing feasibility of new product designs

Creating and managing MBOMs, process flows, routings, work instructions, and other technical documentation using digital tools to ensure accuracy and accessibility

Supporting engineering trials, first builds, and line changes, working closely with production, quality, and planning teams to resolve constraints and ensure smooth transitions

Collaborating with Tooling Engineers and suppliers to ensure timely delivery and validation of production tooling

Actively participating in daily stand-ups, Material Review Boards, and other cross-functional meetings, providing regular updates and flagging delivery risks

Carrying out assessments of manufacturing processes and equipment to ensure compliance with safety standards and operational risk mitigation
•
Executing advanced quality planning activities such as PFMEA and Control Plans, Virtual Builds and Production Readiness Reviews, and validating processes using data-driven methods
•
Supporting FRACAS investigations by applying structured problem-solving techniques to identify root causes and implement corrective actions
•
Contributing accurate manufacturing cost estimates and feasibility assessments to support programmes in the initial proposal phases
•
Taking ownership of personal development by actively seeking feedback, engaging in training, and participating in team development initiatives
•
Contributing to a collaborative team environment by sharing knowledge, supporting peers, and engaging constructively in cross-functional interactions.

•
A degree qualification in Mechanical, Industrial, Manufacturing Engineering, or HNC/HND and relevant experience
•
Proven experience in process design and optimisation, with a focus on aerospace manufacturing and safety-critical components

Detail-oriented and driven by a continuous improvement mindset and a commitment to operational excellence

Understanding of Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DFMA) principles and how to apply them in the early stages of product development

Familiarity with manufacturing automation and industrial equipment, especially related to electro-mechanical assembly and processes such as potting, crimping electrical testing and leak testing

Knowledge of Quality Management Systems (QMS) and typical aerospace quality standards such as ISO9001, AS9100 and AS9145

Competent in ERP/MRP systems (e.g. SAP) and Product Lifecycle Management tools such as Siemens Teamcenter and Opcenter Manufacturing Execution System (MES)

Strong analytical, problem-solving and project management skills with the ability to balance multiple priorities under tight deadlines

The Role:
Joining Moderna means advancing mRNA science to transform medicine. Work with exceptional global teams on a broad pipeline and build a career that makes a real difference for patients.
As Moderna expands its scientific capabilities in the UK, we are seeking a highly skilled bioanalytical scientist to join our Clinical Bioanalytical team. This role sits at the intersection of basic science research, bioanalysis, and clinical development, helping advance innovative mRNA programs through phase-appropriate assay development, qualification, and validation activities.
Working in a highly collaborative environment, you will play a critical role in ensuring robust bioanalytical methodologies are developed and transferred into a GCLP-compliant framework to support clinical programs. This is an opportunity to contribute directly to the generation of high-quality pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic data while working with advanced molecular biology technologies and emerging digital capabilities that are transforming drug development.
Here's What You'll Do:
• Perform bioanalytical assays utilizing a range of molecular and cellular biology techniques, including gel electrophoresis, droplet digital PCR (ddPCR), quantitative PCR (qPCR), RT-qPCR, and related technologies for the quantitation of RNA in biological matrices.
• Support the integration of basic science research and bioanalytical activities to advance development programs into a GCLP-compliant clinical environment.
• Execute phase-appropriate assay development, qualification, and validation activities supporting pharmacokinetic (PK) and pharmacodynamic (PD) analyses.
• Conduct genomic DNA and RNA isolation and apply molecular biology methodologies to generate high-quality analytical data.
• Ensure assays are developed, optimized, qualified, and validated within required timelines to support program milestones and clinical study needs.
• Establish fit-for-purpose bioanalytical methods that meet scientific, regulatory, and GCLP compliance requirements for clinical use.
• Evaluate and review raw analytical data, assay validation reports, and study reports to ensure data integrity, scientific rigor, and compliance with current regulatory, industry, and Moderna standards.
• Partner with internal and external laboratories to ensure analytical activities are performed according to established quality expectations and regulatory requirements.
• Support analytical equipment procurement, qualification, maintenance, and lifecycle management activities.
• Prepare, maintain, and continuously improve Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and supporting documentation.
• Identify, characterize, qualify, and maintain critical reagents required for bioanalytical assay execution and long-term program support.
• Collaborate closely with Clinical Operations, Sample Management, and cross-functional development teams to define sample journeys and develop laboratory manuals that support clinical trial execution.
• Maintain detailed and accurate electronic laboratory notebooks and ensure appropriate documentation practices are consistently followed.
• Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that enhance laboratory efficiency, data quality, compliance, and operational excellence.
• Leverage evolving digital tools, automation technologies, and opportunities to engage with Generative AI-enabled scientific workflows to improve analytical processes and data interpretation.
• Operate effectively within a dynamic, fast-paced environment while demonstrating flexibility, scientific curiosity, and a commitment to team success.
The key Moderna Mindsets you’ll need to succeed in the role:
• We obsess over learning. We don’t have to be the smartest we have to learn the fastest.
• We act with dynamic range, driving strategy and execution at the same time at every step.
Here’s What You’ll Need (Basic Qualifications)
• A M.S with a minimum of 5+ years or B.S with 8+ years in Molecular Biology or relevant scientific discipline of bioanalytical and GCLP/GLP experience in performing clinical molecular assays.
• Hands-on experience with molecular biology and nucleic acid characterization techniques including gel electrophoresis, capillary electrophoresis, and qPCR is highly desired and experience with NGS and genomics is a plus.
• Ability to effectively communicate program objectives, data analysis and present findings to group team members and key stakeholders.
• Knowledge of GCLP requirements and understanding of current industry trends and regulatory expectations associated with analytical science.
• A desire to make an impact as part of a high-growth, transformational company that is Bold, Relentless, Curious, and Collaborative.
Pay & Benefits
At Moderna, we believe that when you feel your best, you can do your best work.  That’s why our benefits and well-being resources are designed to support you—at work, at home, and everywhere in between.
• Competitive healthcare, plus voluntary benefit programs to support your unique needs
• A holistic approach to well-being with access to fitness, mindfulness, and mental health support
• Family building benefits, including fertility, adoption, and surrogacy support
• Generous paid time off, including vacation, bank holidays, volunteer days, sabbatical, global recharge days, and a discretionary year-end shutdown
• Savings and investments to help you plan for the future
• Location-specific perks and extras
The benefits offered may vary depending on the nature of your employment with Moderna and the country where you work.
About Moderna
Since our founding in 2010, we have aspired to build the leading mRNA technology platform, the infrastructure to reimagine how medicines are created and delivered, and a world-class team. We believe in giving our people a platform to change medicine and an opportunity to change the world.
By living our mission, values, and mindsets every day, our people are the driving force behind our scientific progress and our culture. Together, we are creating a culture of belonging and building an organization that cares deeply for our patients, our employees, the environment, and our communities.
We are proud to have been recognized as a Science Magazine Top Biopharma Employer, a Fast Company Best Workplace for Innovators, and a Great Place to Work in the U.S.
As we build our company, we have always believed an in-person culture is critical to our success. Moderna champions the significant benefits of in-office collaboration by embracing a 70/30 work model. This 70% in-office structure helps to foster a culture rich in innovation, teamwork, and direct mentorship. Join us in shaping a world where every interaction is an opportunity to learn, contribute, and make a meaningful impact.

Reporting into our Engineering Manager - Sporting Systems, this role will support the installation, deployment and management of the F1 timing data acquisition and communications system at F1 race locations.
Main Duties and Responsibilities
• Competently install the timing loops, beacons and track temperature sensors in the surface of the track. This involves manual work including digging, soldering, operation of machinery and tools (for which health and safety training will be provided).
• To work in a safe way at all times with consideration to company and location specific Health and Safety requirements.
• Installation, testing and termination of co-axial cable and multi core twisted pair data cable used for loop and decoder data communications.
• Test and verify correct function of all timing data acquisition equipment and related hardware.
• Fault finding on basic IT networks and cable systems.
• Compile and publish reports for the department.
• Be prepared to work in an outdoor environment in a multitude of global destinations.
• Ensure department and company tools and equipment are correctly used, maintained and freighted between races.
• Read, comprehend and work to the F1 Circuit Drawings to achieve the correct equipment setup for a race.
• Learn to configure and monitor incoming and outgoing data using F1 software to ensure correct function of company systems. Report issues to the F100 team and associated clients.
• Mark loop IDs on track with spray paint.
• Install beacon fittings in track and pit lane.
• Mark front axle points for pit-stop boxes in pit lane.
• Configure and deploy the timing decoders, pit lane nodes and workshop furniture.
Other
• Basic data analysis to identify trends and faults.
• Safe loading and unloading of work equipment.
What Are We Looking For?
Personal Qualities
In this role it is essential that you are:
• Well presented, organised and a positive can-do attitude.
• Strong team working ability – capable of working outdoors in both hot and cold weather.
• Ability to travel on a regular basis for extended periods (1 to 3 weeks).
• Willingness to learn new skills and a keen interest in the technical subjects related to the job role.
• Excellent communicator with ability to express oneself accurately and concisely.
• Good time management skills.
Experience
Prior to the role it would be essential that you have:
• Fault finding on electrical/electronic wiring systems.
• Reading, understanding and working to wiring diagrams and technical drawings.
Some desirable experience that you may bring to the role:
• Working knowledge of IP addressing, TCP/IP communications
• Previous experience working in similar environment such as electronics or network IT
Qualifications

Qualifications in Motorsport Engineering with an electrical/electronic bias.

Job Description
A front-row seat to the science of work
When it comes to shaping how one of the UK’s largest organisations works, traditional HR can only take us so far. We need data that leaves no room for guesswork. Technology that keeps people and processes connected. And strategy that’s born out of insight. Exactly what our People & Places teams do every single day.
But they don’t do it alone. Our occupational psychologists are the people behind the people – using behavioural science, research and insight to understand what makes work work better. Join us on the Occupational Psychology Graduate Scheme and see how it all happens up close.
2 years. Three rotations.
You’ll do the hard yards in a training-to-profession scheme that puts you front and centre of occupational psychology in action. And along the way, you’ll:
•
Bring your scientific know-how, insight and creativity to the most important challenges we face as an organisation
•
Understand how psychology is used in a real business setting
•
Help improve performance and wellbeing by improving how we work and make decisions

Throughout the scheme, you’ll find yourself touching a range of projects within the People function. Whether it’s assessment and selection or performance and development, you’ll back every decision you make with data and research. You’ll also:
•
Decode how collaboration, office design and colleague experience can drive engagement, productivity and wellbeing
•
Conduct applied research and lead projects to uncover what drives performance
•
Evaluate our existing people systems and frameworks and understand how we can improve performance management, leadership capability and talent processes
•
Analyse colleague data to explain patterns, challenge assumptions and influence how the organisation functions
•
Create frameworks and guidance that make way for occupational psychology to be used throughout the business
•
Design fair and effective assessments that improve how we evaluate potential, performance and development
And whatever you do, you won’t be doing it alone. A dedicated supervisor will always have your back, so you’ll stay on track with your own development as well. You’ll also have access to a growing community of Occupational Psychologists across the Group, giving you plenty of opportunities to learn and make your mark as part of a function that’s always evolving.
What you’ll take away
By the end of the scheme, you’ll have the skills, the confidence and the experience to apply psychology in a commercial environment – where everything you do will improve how we work together to serve our customers. You’ll also complete a fully funded Stage 2 training, working towards Chartered Psychologist status.

•
Be eligible for the Graduate Basis for Chartered Membership
•
Be currently studying towards or have completed a BPS-accredited Master’s in Occupational Psychology
•
While we do not require a set projected minimum degree achievement, we strongly recommend the ability to be able to demonstrate sound knowledge, understanding and technical skills aligned to the role. Some aspects of this, alongside behaviours and values, will be assessed through the application process.

We cannot sponsor visas.

You’ll select one of these regional locations and will be based in various offices for the duration of your programme. We support hybrid working, where you’ll be expected to spend a minimum of two days each week in the office where you have been placed.

As the global leader in high-speed connectivity, Ciena is committed to a people-first approach. The Data Scientist – Supply Chain Optimisation role applies advanced analytics, operations research, machine learning, and statistical modeling to complex global supply chain challenges that directly influence cost efficiency, service performance, and sustainability outcomes.
How you will make an impact:
•Design and implement operations research and optimization models for network design, inventory positioning, production and capacity planning, sourcing, scheduling, and transportation using linear programming, mixed-integer programming, constraint programming, simulation, heuristics, and metaheuristics.
•Develop and evaluate classical machine learning and statistical models, including regression, classification, clustering, time-series forecasting, probabilistic models, and ensemble methods, to improve supply chain performance, cost efficiency, service levels, and sustainability outcomes.

•Select and apply optimization, machine learning, and statistical approaches to solve complex supply chain problems; validate model performance and assumptions, quantify uncertainty, and communicate trade-offs and recommendations.

•Background working with modern data platforms such as Snowflake and transformation tools such as dbt.
•Exposure to operationalizing machine learning models through repeatable MLOps practices, including experiment tracking, source and model version control, automated testing, deployment pipelines, model registries, production monitoring, drift detection, retraining, rollback, and lifecycle documentation.
•Experience with cloud-based or enterprise machine learning platforms and related engineering practices, including Dataiku, Databricks, Azure Machine Learning/Azure AI, MLflow, containerization, APIs, CI/CD tooling, and production observability.

About AWE
What if you could work with remarkable people on extraordinary things? What if the end result was something a little bit special? What if your role was mission critical?
For over 75 years, AWE has been at the forefront of nuclear weapons research and development. We have a critical mission: to provide the warheads for the UK's ultimate deterrent, Trident. We also use our unique skills to provide wider UK government with counter-terrorism and nuclear threat reduction solutions.
It takes a special sort of person to work at AWE. What if that person was you?
Role purpose
Materials Science supports the life cycle of warhead components and technologies to ensure the reliability of the UK's strategic deterrent and national security mission. A nuclear warhead contains a wide range of materials, including metals, ceramics, inorganic salts, rubbers, foams, adhesives, high explosives and radioactive substances. Materials and Analytical Science is critical to understanding and predicting how these materials behave under different conditions.
As an undergraduate within the Modelling Team in Materials and Analytical Science, you will work on projects involving a range of models and codes, using several coding languages to help deliver AWE's mission.
Key activities
• Work with Materials and Analytical Scientists to characterise material ageing processes and propose approaches to model observed trends.
• Use a variety of statistical techniques to analyse experimental data.
• Write, develop and run code in languages and packages such as MATLAB, Mathematica, OpenFOAM and R.
• Use computational techniques for parameter optimisation.
• Verify and validate codes by identifying suitable test cases and determining analytical solutions where appropriate.

We are interested in candidates working towards a degree in:
• Mathematics, with modelling experience
• Physics
• Computer Science
• Materials Science
• Chemistry, with demonstrable strong mathematics or programming skills
• You must be on track to achieve a minimum 2:2 in your degree by August 2027.
• Most importantly, we are looking for enthusiastic individuals who are keen to get involved in interesting research and tasks.
Behaviours and qualities
You will possess the following traits and qualities:
• Growth mindset: You are full of grit and determination, clear about where you are going and how you will get there.
• Curious: You love to think outside the box, and may even want to take the box apart.
• Innovative: You are open to learning about new technologies and ground-breaking ideas.
• Resilience: You advocate speaking up for yourself and others openly and constructively.
• Team worker: You are dependable and reliable, and interested in collaborating with and supporting others.

• £24,500 salary.
• A market-leading contributory pension scheme.
• Generous holiday entitlement.
• Excellent work-life balance.
• A 9-day working fortnight, meaning you get every other Friday off work.
Alongside these benefits, you will have the opportunity to learn from some of the top leaders in their field.
Recruitment process and key dates
• Online application: Choose the pathway that best matches your interests and goals.
• Online assessment: If eligible, complete numerical, verbal, logical and cognitive reasoning assessments. Practice materials will be available.
• Virtual assessment centre: Successful candidates will be invited to a virtual assessment centre during November or December 2026.
• Pre-assessment support: Receive webinar guidance so you know what to expect.

Security requirements

Inclusion and diversity
Our ambition is to create workplaces where we recognise and celebrate differences, encourage diverse contributions and enable employees to feel able to be themselves at work. We strive to create a genuine culture of openness and inclusion and encourage diverse applicants.
Any inclusion information you provide will be used to encourage and support you through the application process and will be held only for this purpose in accordance with GDPR.

Big responsibility. Personal support. That’s Beyond the Ordinary.
Want to get stuck into client work, tackle complex problems and build your career in Tax? Welcome to the Tax Graduate Programme at BDO.

As for you
You’re inquisitive, resilient and motivated. You enjoy solving problems, thinking things through and learning something new.
You don’t need to arrive knowing everything. Bring your curiosity, logical mindset and willingness to get involved, and you’ll have the support and experience to develop from there.
Join us in Gatwick, Guildford, Reading or Southampton hubs.

• GCSEs at grade 4 and above in Maths and English, or Scottish National 5 grade A-C. You’ll also need to provide evidence if successful
• Commitment to balance study and professional work
• The right to work in the UK (we are unable to provide visa sponsorship for these roles as they do not meet the current minimum salary requirements for sponsorship set by the Home Office. Applications from candidates who have their own legal right to work within the UK must cover the duration of their 3-year training contract and employment)
How the interview process will go
We want you to know what to expect, so here’s the typical process:
• Online application form.
• Online assessments.
• Video interview.
• Virtual assessment centre.
• Final interview in person.
We’ll keep you updated at each stage and share tips to help you prepare. And just so you know: we don’t use AI in any part of our candidate screening process. Every application is reviewed by a real person.
What you get in return
Our benefits are designed to support your life in and outside of work, with options including additional leave, gym membership and employee discounts, alongside pension, health and wellbeing support and a range of protection benefits.

£30,000 - £32,000 per annum depending on location
Closing date for applications is Sunday 15th November 2026
Before you go
Wherever you join BDO, you’ll have the chance to learn by doing, work with clients and build your career with people around you to support your development.
The opportunity to build your experience, confidence and career without having to do it alone.
Big responsibility. Personal support.
That’s Beyond the Ordinary.
Apply now.

Role Overview:
We are looking for a motivated and analytical Graduate Residual Value Analyst to join our team and support residual value (RV) analysis across our international fleet. This is an excellent opportunity for a recent graduate or early-career professional to develop their expertise in automotive finance, vehicle pricing and remarketing.
Working closely with the RV Manager and wider team, you will help analyse vehicle values, monitor used-car market trends and support pricing and fleet investment decisions across a number of countries. You will learn how to apply our central RV methodology to different local markets, using data and market insights to help the business make informed decisions.
The role combines hands-on data analysis, regular reporting and collaboration with teams across Remarketing, Procurement, Finance and Fleet Planning. You will receive guidance and support as you develop your technical skills and commercial understanding.
What You'll Be Doing
• Support residual value forecasting by collecting, analysing and interpreting vehicle market data for your assigned countries.
• Assist with pricing reserve analysis for vehicles being prepared for remarketing, helping the team understand potential resale values.
• Support new-vehicle deal evaluations by analysing proposed vehicle costs, expected residual values and relevant market data.
• Monitor used-vehicle market trends, including changes in vehicle prices, manufacturer incentives, repurchase programmes and wider economic conditions.
• Work with cross-functional teams to gather market information, validate assumptions and support vehicle disposal planning.
• Prepare regular reports and dashboards to track residual value performance and share insights with the RV Manager and wider business.
• Maintain and improve data quality by identifying inconsistencies, investigating anomalies and highlighting potential issues to the team.
• Research electric vehicle (EV) and alternative-fuel residual values, developing an understanding of changing customer demand, regulation and market conditions.
• Carry out ad hoc analysis to support Procurement and Remarketing decisions, helping turn data into clear, practical recommendations.
• Benchmark vehicle values and performance against external data providers, competitor trends and relevant market information.
• Help improve analytical tools and processes, contributing ideas to make reporting more efficient and support the development of our central RV methodology.
• Explore AI and data tools to support research, analysis and report preparation, ensuring all outputs are checked for accuracy.
What You'll Bring
• A university degree in Economics, Finance, Mathematics, Statistics, Data Analytics, Business or a related discipline. Recent graduates are encouraged to apply.
• A strong interest in the automotive industry, vehicle pricing, finance or data analytics.
• Good analytical and numerical skills, with the ability to interpret data, identify trends and draw logical conclusions.
• Good working knowledge of Microsoft Excel, including formulas, data manipulation and pivot tables. Familiarity with Power BI or SQL would be an advantage.

Job Description
Your New Role: Senior Machine Learning Engineer
Global’s central Data Science function is recruiting a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to work across the full breadth of our data and product portfolio.
As a Senior Machine Learning Engineer at Global, you’ll be the engineering bridge between data science and production—taking models built by our data scientists and making them robust, scalable and maintainable across audience targeting, advertising measurement and content intelligence. It’s based in central London (Holborn, with occasional travel to Leicester Square).
Key Responsibilities
•
Model Development, Productionisation & Migration (65%): Translate experimental models into reliable, testable production systems; build APIs and serving infrastructure across batch and real-time; design consistent feature pipelines; and audit and migrate existing models to modern standards without disrupting live products.
•
Standards & Enablement (20%): Define engineering standards for how models are built, tested and deployed, aligned to the MLOps platform, and create reusable templates and documentation that help data scientists work independently.
•
Cross-functional Partnership (15%): Work with data scientists, MLOps, data engineering and product to shape new products early and ensure models are handed off in a deployable, maintainable form.
What You’ll Love About This Role
•
Think Big: This is a true AI and data-driven space—the models you ship influence what millions of listeners hear and how brands invest their media budgets.
•
Own It: You’ll shape how we build going forward, not just maintain what exists—your engineering standards become the team’s standards.
•
Keep it Simple: You’ll build reusable patterns and templates rather than one-off solutions.
•
Better Together: You’ll work across the full range of Global’s data products, partnering with Data Science, MLOps, Data Engineering and Product.
What Success Looks Like
In your first few months, you’ll have:
•
Built a clear understanding of Global’s engineering and data science tools, how they connect, and where ML sits commercially.
•
Established strong working relationships and operating models with Data Science and MLOps.
•
Completed an audit of existing ML models in production, assessing stability, maintainability and risk.
•
Engineered a model to a more robust, documented state and built reusable components others can use.
What You’ll Need
•
Production ML experience: You’ve delivered ML and deep-learning projects at high data volume in commercial environments, owning deployment, CI/CD, monitoring and lifecycle management.
•
Strong Python: Solid Python with PyTorch or similar ML frameworks.
•
Model evaluation: You diagnose why models underperform across data, features and architecture, and make reasoned trade-offs.
•
Real-time ML & reproducibility: A strong grasp of production inference patterns and reproducible environments (Docker, MLflow or equivalent).
•
Cloud & tooling: AWS, plus SageMaker, Snowflake, Spark/Databricks and Kubernetes.
•
Engineering mindset: A focus on reliability, maintainability and continuous improvement.
